title: Breast Surgical Oncology Fellowship

prerequisites.learnerLevel: Postgraduate physician/surgeon self-study; intended for general-surgery graduates or senior trainees who already understand anatomy, pathology, perioperative care, oncology basics and evidence appraisal.
recommendedPriorKnowledge: General surgery breast and oncology foundations
TNM staging and common histopathology terminology
Basic medical statistics and clinical-trial interpretation
prerequisites.programmeEligibilityBoundary: The course does not certify eligibility for a fellowship. The official MGB application page’s precise requirements control any application; ABS rules control ABS eligibility.

objectives: Explain breast surgical oncology presentation, benign/high-risk/malignant differential, imaging/biopsy and radiology-pathology concordance.
Synthesize stage, biology, patient priorities and systemic/radiation therapy interfaces in a multidisciplinary discussion.
Distinguish breast-conserving surgery, mastectomy, margins and axillary evidence within guideline scope.
Recognize special populations, recurrence, implant-related concerns, palliation and survivorship.
Appraise evidence, quality data and source/licensing conditions without claiming clinical competence.
Map learning to published ABS general-surgery and CGSO exam domains while distinguishing those exams from BSO fellowship approval.

units.title: Risk, epidemiology, benign breast disease and the first diagnostic pathway
objectives: Distinguish common benign, high-risk and malignant presentations while maintaining a differential rather than inferring diagnosis from one symptom.
Construct a structured evaluation using history, examination, age/context-appropriate imaging and tissue diagnosis when indicated.
Explain inherited-risk assessment, genetic counseling referral and limits of risk-reducing surgery decisions.
topics: Breast anatomy and epidemiology; breast pain, palpable mass, cyst, fibroadenoma, phyllodes, nipple discharge, mastitis/abscess, granulomatous mastitis, Mondor disease.
High-risk lesions including ADH, ALH, LCIS, FEA and radial scar; concordance and upgrade concepts.
Family history, risk models, genetic counselling, chemoprevention and shared decision-making.
boardDomains: ABS CGSO QE: Breast—benign female breast disorders (12% of all CGSO QE across all breast content); epidemiology; screening/counselling for genetic syndromes.
ABS General Surgery QE: Breast (about 7% of QE); evaluation, oncology/tumor biology, ethics.
units.casePractice: Use one de-identified CBIS-DDSM mass or calcification image set (view at source; do not export or rehost). Pair with a fictional symptom/history card; state what cannot be concluded from a mammogram alone. Dataset pathology annotations are retrospective and are not a diagnostic management pathway.
units.assessment: Create a one-page differential and work-up map for three fictional presentations; label urgent red flags, next diagnostic step, and limits.

units.title: Breast imaging, biopsy, pathology and radiology–pathology concordance
objectives: Interpret the role and limits of screening/diagnostic mammography, ultrasound, MRI and image-guided biopsy in surgical planning.
Use BI-RADS as a standardized reporting framework, not as a substitute for pathology or clinical judgment.
Identify the need to reconcile discordant imaging and pathology with a multidisciplinary team.
topics: Screening versus diagnostic imaging; mammography/DBT, ultrasound, MRI and localization concepts.
Core biopsy, clip/localization concepts, radiology–pathology concordance, benign discordance and repeat sampling/excision consideration.
Histology, grade, ER/PR/HER2 testing, and where pathology review changes management.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast diagnostic workup, imaging, pathology, preoperative evaluation.
ABS GS QE: breast, radiology and preoperative evaluation/perioperative care.
units.casePractice: At TCIA CBIS-DDSM, inspect one authentic de-identified mass and one calcification example with the source-provided labels; make a structured observation list without reproducing images. Discuss limitations of a film-mammography research set and absent clinical context.
units.assessment: Submit a radiology–pathology concordance memo for a clearly labeled fictional scenario; rubric rewards reconciliation and escalation, not a definitive diagnosis.

units.title: In situ, high-risk and uncommon breast neoplasia
objectives: Separate DCIS from invasive carcinoma and classify the questions that pathology, imaging and clinical extent must resolve.
Apply the DCIS margin consensus only within its stated scope and distinguish it from invasive-cancer margin guidance.
Discuss benign/high-risk pathology, LCIS variants and uncommon tumors without overgeneralizing one treatment rule.
topics: DCIS grade, extent, calcifications, margin status and the distinction between local-control choices.
ADH/ALH/LCIS/FEA/radial scars; pathology review and risk implications.
Paget disease, malignant phyllodes, sarcoma, tubular/mucinous/metaplastic and other uncommon histologies.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast benign female disorders and malignant neoplasms; pathology; diagnostic workup.
ABS GS QE: breast; pathology and oncology/tumor biology.
units.casePractice: Use TCIA mammography examples with actual source-provided pathology labels as image interpretation exercises only. For DCIS margin decisions, use fictional pathology text rather than infer microscopic margins from an image dataset.
units.assessment: Compare two fictional margin vignettes—DCIS with whole-breast RT planned versus invasive cancer with RT planned—and state the guideline scope and unresolved patient-specific factors.

units.title: Invasive breast cancer biology, staging and treatment sequencing
objectives: Integrate clinical/anatomic extent, nodal status, grade and receptor/HER2 status into an initial multidisciplinary problem representation.
Distinguish clinical pretreatment stage from post-treatment pathologic staging prefixes.
Compare surgery-first and neoadjuvant pathways as a multidisciplinary decision, without prescribing therapy from this self-study curriculum.
topics: Clinical evaluation, histology, ER/PR/HER2, grade and TNM staging; primary and regional work-up.
Subtype and response-sensitive sequencing; tumor board communication.
Neoadjuvant therapy: baseline extent/biopsy/clip, response assessment and surgical implications.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast malignant neoplasms; pathology; preoperative evaluation; preoperative care/medical care; adjuvant therapy/postoperative care.
ABS GS QE: breast; applied oncology/tumor biology; evaluation/perioperative care.
units.casePractice: Work through a fictional MDT referral using only a short synthetic clinical summary; do not model a treatment recommendation for an actual patient. Use CBIS-DDSM only for imaging-description practice, not for clinical stage.
units.assessment: Produce a tumor-board one-slide summary separating known facts, unknowns, pathology/imaging needs and questions for medical/radiation oncology.

units.title: Breast-conserving surgery, margins, localization and operative standards
objectives: Explain the clinical context in which breast-conserving surgery with radiation and mastectomy are discussed, including patient goals and contraindications.
Apply invasive margin and DCIS margin recommendations to their distinct populations and radiation assumptions.
Describe preoperative localization, specimen orientation, margin communication and quality/outcome review at a conceptual level.
topics: Breast conservation versus mastectomy; multicentricity, inflammatory breast cancer and prior treatment issues.
Invasive carcinoma: no ink on tumor for stages I–II with whole-breast irradiation; wider negative margins generally do not improve local recurrence.
DCIS: 2 mm guideline standard with whole-breast irradiation; <2 mm alone is not a mastectomy indication; treatment without RT has different evidence.
Localization and specimen imaging, cavity shaves, orientation, pathology communication and re-excision decisions.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast malignant neoplasms; intraoperative management; functional/cosmetic optimization; adjuvant therapy.
ABS GS QE: breast; applied oncology; perioperative care; radiology.
units.casePractice: Use fictional pathology reports for margin exercises. Pair with a linked, authentic de-identified TCIA mammogram to practice lesion description only; no image is copied into a handout.
units.assessment: Write a two-part margin interpretation with applicable guideline, scope, and at least three contextual factors that may affect further surgery.

units.title: Mastectomy, oncoplastic planning and reconstruction interfaces
objectives: Compare total/skin-sparing/nipple-sparing approaches at a conceptual level and identify when oncologic extent, risk or patient goals constrain options.
Describe oncoplastic and reconstructive collaboration, patient autonomy and expectation-setting.
Recognize implant safety issues and distinguish breast implant-associated lymphoma from breast carcinoma.
topics: Mastectomy options, skin/nipple involvement, risk-reducing decisions, pathology and reconstruction choices.
Oncoplastic breast-conserving surgery: volume/defect planning, symmetry and communication with plastic surgery.
Implant complications, BIA-ALCL signals, informed choice and long-term follow-up.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast intraoperative management; functional/cosmetic optimization; postoperative care/complications; quality/outcomes.
ABS GS QE: breast and plastic surgery cross-domain; perioperative care.
units.casePractice: Discuss a fictional reconstruction-choice conversation. An optional link to UW teaching files has permission for educational/research use but its portal does not explicitly establish de-identification; do not use its images in course materials or assignments until that is confirmed.
units.assessment: Draft a plain-language shared-decision and referral checklist that lists benefits/risks as questions, avoids guaranteeing outcomes, and preserves patient autonomy.

units.title: Axillary staging, sentinel nodes and evidence-based de-escalation
objectives: Explain the role of sentinel lymph-node biopsy in invasive breast cancer and its morbidity tradeoffs.
Interpret landmark de-escalation evidence only within its inclusion criteria and treatment context.
Communicate nodal pathology and downstream implications with oncology colleagues.
topics: Axillary anatomy, clinical assessment, imaging and needle biopsy.
Sentinel-node procedure principles, mapping, specimen handling and staging.
Omission of completion dissection in evidence-defined populations; older/frailer adults and current guideline review.
Lymphedema, shoulder function, rehabilitation and surveillance.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast intraoperative management; diagnostic workup; adjuvant therapy/postoperative care; rehabilitation.
ABS GS QE: breast; pathology; postoperative complications.
units.casePractice: Use only fictional case summaries for nodal decisions; a CBIS-DDSM image alone cannot establish axillary status. Observe an authentic de-identified mammogram from TCIA and separately state what the image does not show.
units.assessment: For three fictional vignettes, list inclusion/exclusion information needed before applying an axillary de-escalation trial; do not supply an unsupervised procedure plan.

units.title: Neoadjuvant therapy, targeted axillary strategies and response assessment
objectives: Explain why pretreatment baseline imaging/biopsy and marker placement support post-neoadjuvant planning.
Distinguish persistent clinical nodal disease from clinical response and identify the limits of evidence after conversion to clinically node-negative status.
Present an evidence question to a multidisciplinary team rather than extrapolate from a single trial.
topics: Biopsy-confirmed nodal disease and baseline documentation.
Neoadjuvant therapy by receptor subtype; response and residual burden concepts.
Sentinel-node assessment after neoadjuvant therapy, targeted-node retrieval concepts, false-negative risk and current recommendations.
Radiation and systemic therapy interface.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast preoperative care, intraoperative management, adjuvant therapy/postoperative care.
ABS GS QE: breast, applied science/oncology and perioperative care.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional pretreatment and post-treatment timeline. Do not label treatment response from an imaging research dataset without the relevant clinical/protocol context.
units.assessment: Draw a timeline separating cTNM before systemic therapy, response assessment and post-treatment pathology; flag where a current guideline check is needed.

units.title: Hereditary, male, pregnancy-associated and inflammatory breast cancer
objectives: Identify populations that require distinct counseling, imaging, pathology and multidisciplinary pathways.
Distinguish inflammatory breast cancer from ordinary localized disease and recognize its implications for local therapy.
Discuss fertility, lactation, pregnancy and male breast disease without applying female-only assumptions.
topics: BRCA1/2, TP53, PALB2 and other relevant predisposition genes; risk assessment and genetic counseling.
Male breast cancer and hereditary association.
Pregnancy/lactation, postpartum changes, fertility preservation and coordination.
Inflammatory breast cancer, Paget disease and occult primary with nodal presentation.
Older-adult breast oncology: function, comorbidity, competing risks and patient priorities; historical recording only, with current guidance checked separately.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast malignant neoplasms and male breast disease; screening/genetic counselling; epidemiology; health equity.
ABS GS QE: breast; ethics and patient-centered care.
units.casePractice: Use clearly labeled fictional vignettes; for imaging practice only, link to the de-identified TCIA mammography collection and note its modality/clinical-context limits.
units.assessment: Create a referral map for genetics, fertility, medical oncology, radiation oncology and breast imaging; identify the information still needed.

units.title: Local-regional recurrence, metastatic disease, palliation and survivorship
objectives: Differentiate local/regional recurrence from distant metastatic disease and assemble the diagnostic questions before considering local treatment.
Describe surgery as one component of multimodal care and recognize when palliation, rehabilitation or symptom control is central.
Discuss surveillance, lymphedema risk, survivorship and patient-reported outcomes.
topics: Recurrence after BCS or mastectomy; biopsy, extent and receptor reassessment concepts.
Metastatic disease: goals of care and multidisciplinary decisions; avoid reflexive primary-tumor surgery claims.
Palliative intent operations, symptom management and end-of-life communication.
Survivorship, arm function, lymphedema and follow-up.
Older-adult breast oncology: function, comorbidity, competing risks and patient priorities; historical recording only, with current guidance checked separately.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: breast disease, surveillance/follow-up, palliation/pain therapy, rehabilitation and end-of-life care.
ABS GS QE: oncology; geriatric surgery/end-of-life care; outcomes.
units.casePractice: Constructed fictional recurrence and symptom-management scenarios only. Do not use archived imaging to infer an actual treatment plan; use TCIA images solely for image-description learning.
units.assessment: Write a goals-of-care conference brief that separates disease status, patient goals, palliative needs and evidence limitations.

units.title: Pathology, research literacy, clinical trials and quality improvement
objectives: Interpret a clinical study’s population, endpoint, design, bias and applicability before translating it to a surgical decision.
Explain breast specimen and sentinel-node pathology workflow at a conceptual level and communicate questions to pathology.
Design a small quality-improvement audit that protects privacy and does not make a causal claim from uncontrolled data.
topics: Specimen orientation, margin assessment, sentinel-node processing and biomarker reporting interfaces.
Randomized trials, noninferiority, observational evidence, endpoints and absolute versus relative effects.
Quality metrics, complications, re-excision patterns, outcomes and patient-reported outcomes.
IRB, consent, de-identification, clinical-trial ethics and data integrity.
boardDomains: CGSO QE: pathology, clinical trials, ethics/research interpretation, systems-based practice and quality.
ABS GS QE: applied science; biostatistics/evidence; ethics and outcomes.
units.casePractice: Use only TCIA’s intentionally de-identified public dataset and its own metadata; never copy patient-level records, identifiers or images into this curriculum. Dataset reuse requires DOI attribution and CC BY 3.0 terms.
units.assessment: Critique one open guideline/evidence source using population, comparator, endpoint, main caveat and generalizability; propose a privacy-safe QI question.

units.title: Integrated tumor board reasoning, patient communication and board-domain synthesis
objectives: Synthesize benign, diagnostic, staging and treatment-sequencing information in a concise multidisciplinary case presentation.
Use the published ABS content outlines as board-domain maps while stating that a breast fellowship is not a breast board exam.
Deliver a patient-centered explanation that expresses uncertainty and avoids guarantees.
topics: Integrated case formulation and differential diagnosis.
Surgical decision reasoning: extent, margins, nodes, reconstruction, systemic/radiation interfaces.
Patient preferences, health equity, communication and handoffs.
Board status: ABS general-surgery certification versus distinct CGSO certification; SSO/ASBrS fellowship approval and limited ASBrS procedure credentials.
boardDomains: ABS CGSO QE breast section: 12% overall; benign female breast disorders, malignant neoplasms, male breast disease; patient-care dimensions published in the CGSO blueprint.
ABS General Surgery QE breast section: approximately 7%; outline updated January 2021. Current annual exam requirements must be checked at the board source.
units.casePractice: Present a fully fictional synthetic tumor-board vignette. If adding an image, link—not copy—to a de-identified TCIA study and cite the DOI/CC BY 3.0; never include patient records.
units.assessment: Final integrated oral/written board-style case: document assumptions, state evidence scope, identify unknowns, communicate a safe next discussion step and avoid procedure authorization.

assignment.title: Integrated multidisciplinary breast case and evidence memo (fictional case + linked image observation)
assignment.prompt: Use a clearly labeled fictional case summary and, optionally, a linked CBIS-DDSM image viewed only at TCIA. Submit a concise tumor-board memo with: problem representation; what is known/unknown; differential or pathology/imaging concordance questions; stage and receptor information required; evidence scope for surgery/margins/axilla; team referrals; patient goals and unresolved questions. Do not supply a real patient treatment plan, procedural steps or a guaranteed outcome. Do not embed, download or redistribute any image or patient-level record.

rubric.meets: Separates known facts from missing data, forms a coherent differential, avoids claiming diagnosis from an image alone.
Names source, target population, intervention, comparator/outcome where relevant; applies margin/axillary recommendations only within scope.
Addresses radiology, pathology, medical and radiation oncology, reconstruction/rehabilitation or genetics as appropriate.
Reflects goals, equity, risks and uncertainty; avoids guarantees or real-world advice.
Cites sources, links to images at source, gives TCIA DOI/CC BY 3.0 attribution if using data, copies no image or record.

assignment.passingThreshold: 70/100 for this educational assignment only; not validated as a predictor of board performance or clinical competence.

assessment.formative: Each unit ends with a short concept check and self-explanation of the applicable evidence boundary. Unit exercises may use fictional cases or linked source images, never patient records copied into this course.
assessment.rubric: Reasoning, appropriate scope, communication, evidence quality, correct identification of unknowns and rights-compliant source use. A passing course score would indicate only completion of these educational tasks; it does not predict board passage or competence.
assessment.validationStatus: Questions are original educational items and have not been validated, psychometrically tested, or reviewed by a human clinician.

mapping.name: Breast Surgical Oncology Fellowship
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Current public MGB page describes a 12-month clinical oncology fellowship based at Massachusetts General Hospital with rotations at Brigham and Women’s Hospital and Dana-Farber Cancer Institute; focus includes breast cancer and benign breast disease, multidisciplinary planning and clinical/basic research. The current page states application/eligibility details. SSO/ASBrS list a Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute breast fellowship as approved. This is the joint offering, not three independent fellowships.

topicGaps: The packet started with 0 verified external hours. Three unique, free-to-view public recordings with observed YouTube player runtimes add 8,551 seconds (2.375278 hours). The 36-hour target remains short by 33.624722 verified hours; planned scripts do not count.

The four original relevant video records remain duration-unknown (V-ACS-OPS, V-ESSO-MARGINS, V-ESSO-ONCOPLASTIC, V-AXILLA); they remain excluded. Do not infer duration from transcript timestamps or title.

Source-backed instruction remains thin or incomplete for benign/high-risk disease and genetics; imaging/biopsy workflow and concordance; DCIS and uncommon histology; current staging and biomarker algorithms; operative localization/specimen practice; oncoplastic/reconstruction depth; targeted axillary approaches after neoadjuvant therapy; hereditary/male/pregnancy-associated/inflammatory disease; recurrence/palliation/survivorship; pathology, trial appraisal, QI, and integrated tumor-board handoff.

The public additions are complementary, not comprehensive: the McGill recording is a specialist translational TNBC-research lecture; the MSK recording is a patient-facing multidisciplinary overview; the UNC grand rounds are from 2010 and historical only. medical.boardStatus: No separate ABS/ABMS board certification or board examination in Breast Surgical Oncology was identified in the reviewed authoritative sources. ABS lists General Surgery and Complex General Surgical Oncology (CGSO) as separate certifications. The SSO/ASBrS-approved Breast Surgical Oncology fellowship is not itself an ABS board examination and does not confer board certification, supervised training or ABS exam eligibility. ASBrS separately offers limited breast ultrasound and stereotactic-procedure certifications; these are not a board specialty. ABS CGSO eligibility requires separate ACGME-accredited CGSO training and prior general-surgery certification. Verify all eligibility directly with the relevant board.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent educational course grants no ABS/ABMS eligibility, licensure, certification, clinical privileges or procedural competence. Preserve the source wording and contact the programme for any ambiguity. ABS general-surgery certification requires its own accredited training and examinations. ABS CGSO certification is a distinct pathway, requiring ACGME-accredited CGSO training and general-surgery certification; this BSO fellowship is not represented as CGSO training.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional multidisciplinary conference reviews a patient with appropriately selected early-stage invasive breast cancer. The person is considering breast-conserving surgery with radiation or mastectomy. Which statement best describes comparative survival in the evidence summarized by NCI?

options.text: Mastectomy always improves overall survival.

For appropriately selected patients in randomized studies, breast-conserving surgery plus radiation and mastectomy have shown equivalent survival; eligibility and patient-specific factors still matter.
Breast conservation is appropriate for all histologies and presentations.
Radiation is never part of breast-conserving treatment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI summarizes equivalent survival in randomized comparisons for the relevant selected populations, but this is not universal eligibility; inflammatory breast cancer is identified as a contraindication to breast-conserving therapy.
practiceQuestions.domain: Breast malignant neoplasms; preoperative evaluation and shared treatment planning

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional stage I invasive carcinoma was excised with no tumor touching ink. Whole-breast irradiation is planned. Under the SSO–ASTRO invasive-cancer margin consensus, which statement is most accurate?

options.text: A negative margin must be at least 10 mm.
No ink on tumor is the adequate negative-margin definition in this guideline scope; wider negative margins have not significantly reduced recurrence.
Any margin less than 2 mm mandates mastectomy.
The invasive-cancer guideline applies only when radiation is omitted.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline applies to stages I/II invasive disease treated with breast-conserving surgery and whole-breast irradiation, and defines negative as no ink on tumor. Scope matters.
practiceQuestions.domain: Breast malignant neoplasms; pathology; intraoperative/postoperative management

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional pure DCIS excision has a negative 1-mm margin; whole-breast irradiation is planned. What does the SSO–ASTRO–ASCO DCIS guideline support?

options.text: A 1-mm margin automatically requires mastectomy.
Two millimeters is the standard adequate margin in this setting, but a negative margin under 2 mm alone does not mandate mastectomy; use clinical judgment about further surgery.
The invasive-cancer no-ink guideline replaces all DCIS margin guidance.
Margins do not affect local recurrence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The DCIS consensus supports a 2-mm standard with whole-breast RT; <2 mm alone is not an indication for mastectomy, and clinical context guides any re-excision decision.
practiceQuestions.domain: Breast malignant neoplasms; pathology; postoperative care

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has biopsy-confirmed invasive breast cancer and clinically negative nodes. According to the NCI PDQ summary, what is the initial standard axillary staging procedure?

options.text: Routine complete axillary dissection in every patient.
Sentinel lymph-node biopsy as the initial standard axillary staging procedure.
No nodal staging is ever used.
Radiation imaging alone replaces nodal staging in every case.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI identifies sentinel lymph-node biopsy as the initial standard axillary staging procedure for invasive cancer; the extent of intervention depends on eligibility and current evidence.
practiceQuestions.domain: Breast malignant neoplasms; diagnostic work-up; intraoperative management

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional diagnostic biopsy has an equivocal HER2 immunohistochemistry result scored 2+. What is the most appropriate interpretation of the NCI summary of current testing criteria?

options.text: HER2 is definitively positive on the basis of IHC 2+ alone.
IHC 2+ is equivocal; interpret with in-situ hybridization testing and the applicable testing algorithm.
HER2 status is irrelevant to multidisciplinary treatment planning.
The result can be replaced by the radiologist’s BI-RADS category.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ labels IHC 2+ equivocal and describes ISH criteria/confirmatory testing. Imaging categories do not determine receptor biomarkers.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient’s pretreatment clinical breast-cancer stage is recorded before neoadjuvant systemic therapy. A learner asks whether the later surgical specimen retroactively replaces that pretreatment clinical stage. Which statement is best?

options.text: Neoadjuvant therapy erases the pretreatment clinical stage.
The pretreatment clinical stage remains the clinical stage; post-treatment findings are separately documented with the appropriate post-therapy prefix and response context.
Clinical and pathologic stages are always identical.
Only the imaging report can assign stage.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI describes pretreatment clinical stage and the use of the yp prefix for post-neoadjuvant pathologic findings. Baseline and response information are both relevant.
practiceQuestions.domain: Breast malignant neoplasms; preoperative evaluation; pathology

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with a breast implant presents years later with persistent unilateral swelling and a peri-implant fluid collection. Which educational response best reflects FDA advice?

options.text: Assume ordinary breast carcinoma and proceed without assessing the fluid.
Consider BIA-ALCL in the differential and refer for expert evaluation; FDA describes cytologic assessment of seroma with CD30/ALK testing among diagnostic evaluations.
Assume the implant is saline, so BIA-ALCL is excluded.
Recommend routine removal of all asymptomatic implants.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA describes persistent swelling, mass or pain as possible symptoms, and recommends a diagnostic assessment of fluid/tissue for suspected cases with expert coordination. It does not recommend routine removal of asymptomatic implants.
practiceQuestions.domain: Breast postoperative complications; diagnostic workup; device safety

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes BIA-ALCL from breast carcinoma and summarizes FDA’s implant-surface qualifier?

options.text: BIA-ALCL is a type of breast epithelial carcinoma and risk is higher with smooth implants.
BIA-ALCL is a non-Hodgkin lymphoma associated with breast implants; FDA states risk is higher with textured than smooth implants.
BIA-ALCL occurs only in saline-filled implants.
FDA advises prophylactic implant removal for every asymptomatic patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA identifies BIA-ALCL as a lymphoma rather than breast cancer, notes higher risk with textured versus smooth implant surfaces, and does not recommend routine removal in asymptomatic patients.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best characterizes certification after completion of a Breast Surgical Oncology Fellowship?

options.text: Completion automatically confers an ABS breast-surgery subspecialty board certificate.
The SSO/ASBrS-approved fellowship is distinct from ABS board certification; ABS lists general surgery and CGSO among certifications, while ASBrS also offers narrower procedure certifications.
The breast fellowship itself is the ABS CGSO certification pathway.
A fellowship title guarantees board eligibility and a passing exam result.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SSO and ASBrS jointly approve BSO fellowship programmes. ABS lists general surgery and complex general surgical oncology certification; CGSO requires separate accredited CGSO training and prior general-surgery certification. ASBrS credentials in breast ultrasound/stereotactic procedures are limited procedural certifications, not a breast board specialty.
practiceQuestions.domain: Certification literacy; professional roles and scope

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner asks how the ABS CGSO QE blueprint weights breast content. Which answer matches the published blueprint, while correctly limiting what that means for this one-year breast fellowship?

options.text: Breast is 12% of all CGSO QE questions, including benign female disorders, malignant neoplasms and male breast disease; this is a CGSO examination map, not a separate BSO board exam.
Breast is 100% of all ABS examination questions.
The CGSO QE blueprint is a breast-fellowship curriculum and the fellowship qualifies any learner to sit it.
The ABS publishes no breast content category.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABS CGSO blueprint lists breast at 12% of all questions and names benign female breast disorders, malignant neoplasms and male breast disease. CGSO eligibility requires distinct accredited training and general-surgery certification.

title: Advanced Gastrointestinal Minimally Invasive Surgery and Bariatrics Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship; independent educational curriculum, not a training appointment-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Completed medical degree and general-surgery residency-level knowledge; this self-study course cannot validate these prerequisites.
Working knowledge of GI anatomy/physiology, perioperative care, basic surgical evidence appraisal and bariatric procedure configurations.
Access to current clinical supervision for any practice questions; no procedural execution or patient care is authorized.
objectives: Map the published ABS MBS FPD exam content outline to 12 cognitive-learning units.
Compare current open professional guidelines and their certainty/scope.
Reason through fictional cases without inventing diagnoses, clinical eligibility, or individual care recommendations.
Distinguish MGB programme facts, Fellowship Council requirements, ABS/AOBS credentials, and independent self-study.
Identify quality, safety, evidence, and ethics questions for bariatric/foregut/hernia services.

units.title: Obesity biology, indications, and shared decision-making
objectives: Explain obesity as chronic disease and distinguish BMI thresholds from individual operative selection.
Apply 2022 ASMBS/IFSO indication recommendations with population/context qualifiers.
Structure shared decision discussions around expected benefits, risks, alternatives, values, and uncertainty.
topics: Obesity pathophysiology; BMI limitations; access/equity and weight stigma; indications and contraindications; multidisciplinary assessment; nonoperative options.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD I: science of obesity (7.5%)
ABS MBS FPD II: indications, preoperative assessment (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional adult with BMI 34 kg/m² and metabolic disease: compare guideline eligibility language, previous treatment, patient priorities, and missing assessment without deciding candidacy from BMI alone.
units.assessment: Short evidence-translation memo; rubric: guideline fidelity 40%, uncertainty/context 30%, shared decision framing 20%, citations 10%.

units.title: Preoperative bariatric evaluation and perioperative risk
objectives: Build a structured preoperative problem list and multidisciplinary assessment map.
Identify anesthesia, cardiopulmonary, functional, psychosocial, and endoscopic workup considerations.
Use risk tools as aids rather than substitutes for clinical judgment or informed consent.
topics: Medical/surgical history, nutrition, behavioral health, OSA, cardiometabolic disease, anesthetic planning, consent, MBSAQIP systems.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD II: preoperative assessment/management, anesthesia, endoscopy, center components (30%)
units.casePractice: Use ACS public calculator with an explicitly fictional profile and critique input/limits; no individualized care recommendation.
units.assessment: Risk-case worksheet; rubric: relevant risks 35%, appropriate testing questions 25%, tool limitations 20%, communication 20%.

units.title: Operative anatomy, access, equipment, and MIS judgment
objectives: Relate foregut and abdominal-wall anatomy to common laparoscopic/robotic procedure choices.
Describe platform/instrument energy hazards and team/safety factors conceptually.
Compare advantages and trade-offs of laparoscopic, robotic, open, and endoscopic approaches.
topics: Anatomy and reconstruction principles, setup, ergonomics, port strategy, surgical energy, patient positioning, conversion readiness.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD III: procedures/devices/safety (25%); broad GI MIS cognitive knowledge (not a separate board exam)
units.casePractice: Annotated schematic exercise using a learner-drawn generic anatomy diagram; not patient imaging or operative instruction.
units.assessment: Approach-comparison brief; rubric: anatomy 30%, safety 30%, tradeoffs 25%, scope limits 15%.

units.title: Sleeve gastrectomy: outcomes, physiology, and reflux trade-offs
objectives: Describe sleeve reconstruction at a cognitive/diagrammatic level and distinguish outcome domains.
Recognize postoperative reflux and other complications as assessment questions, not diagnoses from a single symptom.
Compare published evidence to patient factors without implying universal procedure superiority.
topics: Sleeve anatomy and mechanism; reflux, weight response, complications, long-term follow-up; comparative outcome interpretation.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD III (25%); IV postoperative management (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional postoperative patient reports new reflux; build a differential and testing/evaluation questions; do not prescribe.
units.assessment: Evidence table contrasting procedure-specific outcomes; rubric: accurate comparison 40%, confounding/limits 25%, appropriate evaluation 25%, citations 10%.

units.title: RYGB, SADI/DS, OAGB, and revisional reconstruction
objectives: Compare bypass and diversion configurations, metabolic intent, and potential nutritional consequences.
Interpret limb-length evidence without converting one recording into a universal technical prescription.
Recognize altered anatomy implications for future endoscopy and revision planning.
topics: RYGB; BPD/DS; SADI variants; OAGB; limb length and outcomes; internal hernia conceptual anatomy; revisions.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD III procedures/reconstruction (25%); IV revisions (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional longitudinal case asks what additional anatomy, symptoms, nutrition, and prior-operation records are needed before considering revision.
units.assessment: Reconstruction comparison map; rubric: anatomical accuracy 35%, tradeoffs 30%, altered-anatomy implications 25%, uncertainty 10%.

units.title: GERD, hiatal hernia, and foregut physiology
objectives: Map symptom assessment to objective testing questions for medically refractory GERD.
Summarize SAGES conditional recommendation and uncertainty around hiatal repair/fundoplication/mesh.
Distinguish obesity-related procedure choice as individualized shared decision-making.
topics: Endoscopy, manometry, pH testing; fundoplication; hiatal hernia types; mesh uncertainty; recurrent hernia and RYGB context; GERD after sleeve.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD II endoscopic assessment (30%); III operations (25%); IV complications (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional adult with reflux and hiatal hernia imaging: state what data are missing and what current guideline does and does not recommend.
units.assessment: Guideline appraisal; rubric: recommendation grade/conditionality 35%, test reasoning 30%, values/shared-decision 25%, citations 10%.

units.title: Nutrition, micronutrients, and longitudinal follow-up
objectives: Explain lifelong follow-up and why procedure anatomy changes deficiency risk.
Read an open nutrition guideline critically and identify its date/scope limits.
Design a monitoring-plan template without issuing treatment orders.
topics: Baseline nutrition, protein, iron, B12, folate, thiamine, calcium/vitamin D and fat-soluble nutrients as relevant; adherence; pregnancy context.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD IV postoperative routine/other complications (30%); V special populations (7.5%)
units.casePractice: Fictional patient with fatigue and prior bypass: develop a differential/checklist for nutritional and non-nutritional evaluation; do not infer deficiency.
units.assessment: Monitoring framework; rubric: anatomy-linked risks 35%, breadth 30%, follow-up continuity 20%, explicit limits 15%.

units.title: Early postoperative complications and rescue reasoning
objectives: Organize differential categories for early deterioration after bariatric surgery.
Prioritize escalation/urgent evaluation concepts while avoiding remote diagnosis or treatment instructions.
Separate complication recognition from unsupported procedural prescriptions.
topics: Leak/bleeding/obstruction/thromboembolism/infection/respiratory issues; altered postoperative anatomy; multidisciplinary escalation and quality review.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD IV early complications and management (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional day-two deterioration vignette: describe red flags, high-level differential, and urgent local team assessment need.
units.assessment: Complication concept map; rubric: safety/escalation 40%, differential 25%, anatomy/context 20%, avoids treatment overreach 15%.

units.title: Late complications, weight recurrence, and revision decisions
objectives: Distinguish weight recurrence from inadequate initial response conceptually and identify multifactorial contributors.
Construct evaluation domains before considering endoscopic, medical, behavioral, or surgical options.
Explain increased complexity/risks in revision and the need for multidisciplinary review.
topics: Weight recurrence, reflux, ulcers, internal hernia/obstruction, nutritional issues, altered anatomy, medication options, endoscopic/surgical revision.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD IV other complications, revisions, suboptimal response (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional patient years after bypass with weight recurrence: ask what anatomy, follow-up, behavioral, medication, nutritional, and comorbidity data are missing.
units.assessment: Multidomain case conference note; rubric: differential breadth 30%, evidence-based options 30%, risks 20%, shared decision 20%.

units.title: Hernia and abdominal-wall disease in obesity
objectives: Identify optimization and anatomical factors relevant to ventral/incisional hernia planning.
Summarize EHS guideline scope limitations and avoid extending recommendations beyond its eligible hernias.
Discuss staged versus combined strategy as an individualized question, not a universal rule.
topics: Incisional hernia risk factors, closure/repair concepts, recurrence, obesity, timing relative to MBS, abdominal wall reconstruction, robotic/laparoscopic/open approaches.
boardDomains: Advanced GI MIS cognitive coverage; ABS MBS FPD II/III/IV overlap only where relevant; no separate board exam claimed.
units.casePractice: Fictional patient with severe obesity and a reducible midline incisional hernia: map relevant factors and limits of EHS guideline population.
units.assessment: Guideline applicability memo; rubric: scope fidelity 35%, risk analysis 30%, options 20%, uncertainty 15%.

units.title: Special populations: pregnancy, adolescents, older adults, and comorbidity
objectives: Identify special-population domains that modify assessment, timing, counseling, and follow-up.
Summarize the guideline approach to adolescents and pregnancy-related considerations without substituting for specialty guidance.
Recognize evidence gaps and individualize educational case analysis.
topics: Age-specific populations, pregnancy/fertility/lactation, major comorbidities, frailty, adolescent multidisciplinary assessment.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD V: special populations (7.5%); II preoperative care (30%)
units.casePractice: Fictional learner chooses one context and creates consultation questions for the multidisciplinary team; no eligibility assertions.
units.assessment: Case memo; rubric: population-specific risks 35%, guideline/context 30%, follow-up 20%, limits 15%.

units.title: Quality, registry, scholarly appraisal, and board-style integration
objectives: Explain center quality/accreditation and the difference between a center program and individual board credential.
Apply PICO/GRADE reasoning to guidelines and identify outcome measures and evidence limits.
Map study questions to ABS MBS FPD published domains while distinguishing this course from board preparation guarantee.
topics: MBSAQIP purpose; quality indicators; registry/risk calculator limitations; guideline appraisal; exam blueprint; research literacy; professional boundaries.
boardDomains: ABS MBS FPD I-V; exact weights per published outline: 7.5%, 30%, 25%, 30%, 7.5% (rounded total 100%)
units.casePractice: Fictional QI scenario: identify denominator, outcomes, risk adjustment needs, and governance/limitations without using patient records.
units.assessment: Capstone evidence dossier; rubric: source quality 30%, domain coverage 25%, reasoning 25%, ethics/limits 20%.

assignment.title: Evidence-to-decision portfolio
assignment.instructions: For three fictional cases (one preoperative, one postoperative complication, one foregut/hernia decision), submit a one-page evidence map each with source date, guideline scope, facts versus assumptions, missing information, differential/decision domains, patient values, and safe limits. No individual treatment plan or operative steps.

components: 10 original formative questions with answer rationales
assessment.scoringPlan: Suggested educational self-assessment only: pass threshold 80% on course quiz with remediation and source review; not validated, not a predictor of board passing, not official ABS content, no credential or certificate.
assessment.rubric: Apply unit-specific rubrics; grade evidence use, uncertainty, reasoning, scope boundaries and clarity—not clinical decision authority.

studyHours.note: Suggested self-study plan only, not clinical duty hours or recorded-video hours: 12 units × approximately 4 hours (48), readings and notes (12), assessments/portfolio (12). mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official MGB page describes a one-year, full-time clinical Fellowship Council-accredited fellowship after general surgical training; rotations at Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Massachusetts General Hospital and community affiliates; stated scope includes primary/revisional bariatrics, foregut, abdominal wall/hernia, laparoscopic, robotic and flexible endoscopic procedures, and research/teaching. Official page says two fellows and approximately 350 major operative cases, with estimates stated by program—not independently verified nor guaranteed. Fellowship Council directory says the hospitals combined in 2025 into the integrated MGB department; its live listing simultaneously displays “Pending for Advanced GI MIS/Bariatrics” and approximate 350–400 cases as primary surgeon. This conflicts with MGB’s accreditation statement; accreditation status and case metrics should be reconfirmed directly. Historical separate BWH/MGH programmes have been integrated; retain institution names as rotation sites rather than duplicate tracks.

unitMap.text: Obesity biology, indications, and shared decision-making
coveredTopics: Obesity pathophysiology; BMI limitations; access/equity and weight stigma; indications and contraindications; multidisciplinary assessment; nonoperative options.

unitMap.text: Preoperative bariatric evaluation and perioperative risk
coveredTopics: Medical/surgical history, nutrition, behavioral health, OSA, cardiometabolic disease, anesthetic planning, consent, MBSAQIP systems.

unitMap.text: Operative anatomy, access, equipment, and MIS judgment
coveredTopics: Anatomy and reconstruction principles, setup, ergonomics, port strategy, surgical energy, patient positioning, conversion readiness.

unitMap.text: Sleeve gastrectomy: outcomes, physiology, and reflux trade-offs
coveredTopics: Sleeve anatomy and mechanism; reflux, weight response, complications, long-term follow-up; comparative outcome interpretation.

unitMap.text: RYGB, SADI/DS, OAGB, and revisional reconstruction
coveredTopics: RYGB; BPD/DS; SADI variants; OAGB; limb length and outcomes; internal hernia conceptual anatomy; revisions.

unitMap.text: GERD, hiatal hernia, and foregut physiology
coveredTopics: Endoscopy, manometry, pH testing; fundoplication; hiatal hernia types; mesh uncertainty; recurrent hernia and RYGB context; GERD after sleeve.

unitMap.text: Nutrition, micronutrients, and longitudinal follow-up
coveredTopics: Baseline nutrition, protein, iron, B12, folate, thiamine, calcium/vitamin D and fat-soluble nutrients as relevant; adherence; pregnancy context.

unitMap.text: Early postoperative complications and rescue reasoning
coveredTopics: Leak/bleeding/obstruction/thromboembolism/infection/respiratory issues; altered postoperative anatomy; multidisciplinary escalation and quality review.

unitMap.text: Late complications, weight recurrence, and revision decisions
coveredTopics: Weight recurrence, reflux, ulcers, internal hernia/obstruction, nutritional issues, altered anatomy, medication options, endoscopic/surgical revision.

unitMap.text: Hernia and abdominal-wall disease in obesity
coveredTopics: Incisional hernia risk factors, closure/repair concepts, recurrence, obesity, timing relative to MBS, abdominal wall reconstruction, robotic/laparoscopic/open approaches.

unitMap.text: Special populations: pregnancy, adolescents, older adults, and comorbidity
coveredTopics: Age-specific populations, pregnancy/fertility/lactation, major comorbidities, frailty, adolescent multidisciplinary assessment.

unitMap.text: Quality, registry, scholarly appraisal, and board-style integration
coveredTopics: MBSAQIP purpose; quality indicators; registry/risk calculator limitations; guideline appraisal; exam blueprint; research literacy; professional boundaries.

topicGaps: HPB/solid-organ overlap and flexible-endoscopy procedural breadth remain only partially covered; no dedicated verified HPB/ERCP long-form lecture was added.

Advanced abdominal-wall reconstruction and complex incisional/parastomal hernia technique remain undercovered; the added bariatric hernia recording is not a substitute for a full abdominal-wall curriculum.
MIS/robotics ergonomic and platform concepts are represented, but energy-device hazards, setup, conversion readiness, and hands-on proficiency lack a complete standalone verified recording.
Foregut physiology and objective reflux testing are covered through guideline reading and limited recordings; comprehensive manometry/pH interpretation teaching remains a gap.
Current longitudinal micronutrient monitoring beyond the 2016 ASMBS update needs contemporary source review; recordings do not establish a current protocol.
Program quality, registry denominator/risk-adjustment methods, and current ABS/AOBS eligibility require further primary-source verification and supervised appraisal.
Primary and revisional procedure recordings are broad, but evidence comparisons across OAGB, revision indications, long-term outcomes, and technical variants remain uneven.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship; independent educational curriculum, not a training appointment
boardNames: American Board of Surgery (ABS): General Surgery certification; ABS Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Focused Practice Designation Examination (a designation exam, not a new specialty board certificate)

American Osteopathic Board of Surgery (AOBS): eligible AOBS-certified surgeons take the same MBS FPD exam as eligible ABS diplomates beginning with the 2025 exam; AOBS calls its award a certificate of added qualification.
medical.boardStatus: The MGB fellowship is not itself a board specialty and no distinct board examination for this Advanced GI MIS/Bariatrics fellowship was identified. The ABS MBS Focused Practice Designation examination is a distinct examination for eligible general surgeons, not a new specialty/subspecialty certificate. Beginning with 2025, eligible AOBS-certified and ABS-certified surgeons take the same MBS FPD exam; AOBS recognizes its diplomates with a certificate of added qualification and ABS recognizes its diplomates with a focused practice designation. General Surgery ABS certification is separate. Fellowship Council accreditation/designation is a training-program framework, not an individual board examination.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This curriculum does not make learners eligible for any exam. ABS MBS FPD eligibility requires current ABS general surgery certification, experience/practice/privilege/case requirements and other published criteria; an MBS fellowship year may count toward the clinical-experience requirement but does not itself award designation. Fellowship eligibility, state licensure, certification and operative competency must be verified directly with official bodies.

officialProgrammes.institution: Mass General Brigham (integrated Department of Surgery; Harvard-affiliated teaching hospitals)
officialProgrammes.name: Advanced GI Minimally Invasive Surgery and Bariatrics Fellowship at Mass General Brigham
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official MGB page describes a one-year, full-time clinical Fellowship Council-accredited fellowship after general surgical training; rotations at Brigham and Women’s Hospital, Massachusetts General Hospital and community affiliates; stated scope includes primary/revisional bariatrics, foregut, abdominal wall/hernia, laparoscopic, robotic and flexible endoscopic procedures, and research/teaching. Official page says two fellows and approximately 350 major operative cases, with estimates stated by program—not independently verified nor guaranteed. Fellowship Council directory says the hospitals combined in 2025 into the integrated MGB department; its live listing simultaneously displays “Pending for Advanced GI MIS/Bariatrics” and approximate 350–400 cases as primary surgeon. This conflicts with MGB’s accreditation statement; accreditation status and case metrics should be reconfirmed directly. Historical separate BWH/MGH programmes have been integrated; retain institution names as rotation sites rather than duplicate tracks.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This packet is for the specific MGB clinical physician fellowship listed in the MED-X038 discovery packet. It is not a separate “bariatric surgery board specialty,” nor a generic specialty-directory category, a non-physician/research-only course, or a combined board program. Institutional affiliate relationship is not course sponsorship or endorsement. MGB official page describes a combined clinical fellowship and multidisciplinary research/education obligations. Exact prior legacy programme variants were not independently verified; see current directory note.
sourceCaveats: MGB official program page states Fellowship Council accredited; Fellowship Council directory’s live MGB listing still labels accreditation “Pending for Advanced GI MIS/Bariatrics.” Contradiction unresolved; check directly with both bodies before relying on current status.

Public directory presents approximately 350–400 cases, whereas official MGB page says approximately 350 major operative cases; these are programme-reported estimates, not verified case logs or learner guarantees.
Fellowship Council page contains future/current cycle case reporting (2026–2027); not treated as actual accumulated volume.
ABS FPD content outline itself is dated 11/2021; latest ABS eligibility page checked 2026-10-07. Confirm current board documents before using.
ASMBS nutrition PDF is older (2016 update/2017 publication); it is included with explicit date caveat rather than described as the latest standard.
SAGES Vimeo-linked webinar pages were not counted because direct runtime/playback could not be independently verified without login; no stateful browser or credentials used.
The counted ASMBS media pages show explicit Duration and link to a public ASMBS YouTube channel; playback itself was not exercised. Public video viewing does not confer certificate/CME/board credit.
No original clips are recorded/rendered. All 16 clip plans are proposed production; their target minutes do not count toward video hours.
No protected board questions, private records, rehosted clinical images, or proprietary/log-in-only course items were used.
No human clinical review performed; verify indications, guidelines, board eligibility and licensure with current sources and local governance.

topicGaps: HPB/solid-organ overlap and flexible-endoscopy procedural breadth remain only partially covered; no dedicated verified HPB/ERCP long-form lecture was added.

Advanced abdominal-wall reconstruction and complex incisional/parastomal hernia technique remain undercovered; the added bariatric hernia recording is not a substitute for a full abdominal-wall curriculum.
MIS/robotics ergonomic and platform concepts are represented, but energy-device hazards, setup, conversion readiness, and hands-on proficiency lack a complete standalone verified recording.
Foregut physiology and objective reflux testing are covered through guideline reading and limited recordings; comprehensive manometry/pH interpretation teaching remains a gap.
Current longitudinal micronutrient monitoring beyond the 2016 ASMBS update needs contemporary source review; recordings do not establish a current protocol.
Program quality, registry denominator/risk-adjustment methods, and current ABS/AOBS eligibility require further primary-source verification and supervised appraisal.
Primary and revisional procedure recordings are broad, but evidence comparisons across OAGB, revision indications, long-term outcomes, and technical variants remain uneven.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best reflects the 2022 ASMBS/IFSO guideline for adults?

options.text: MBS is recommended for BMI >35 kg/m² regardless of comorbidity presence/severity.
MBS is recommended only for BMI >40 kg/m².
BMI 30–34.9 universally requires surgery.
BMI alone determines eligibility and procedure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends MBS for BMI >35 regardless of comorbidity severity and says it should be considered for BMI 30–34.9 in metabolic disease; candidacy still requires individualized assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: For typical symptoms of medically refractory GERD before invasive treatment, what does the multi-society guideline suggest?

options.text: Endoscopy, manometry, and pH testing; severe LA C/D esophagitis may obviate pH solely to confirm GERD.
CT alone.
No testing if symptoms respond to antacids.
Manometry only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline suggests endoscopy, manometry, and pH testing; it notes LA C/D esophagitis may mean pH testing is not needed merely for confirmation.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the SAGES panel position on routine mesh for type II–IV hiatal hernia repair?

options.text: No evidence-based recommendation for or against mesh.
Strongly recommends mesh in every repair.
Strongly prohibits mesh.
Recommends mesh only in recurrent cases.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The panel explicitly made no evidence-based recommendation because evidence is insufficient; mesh decisions remain individualized.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which hiatal hernia repair statement is most accurate?

options.text: SAGES suggests routinely performing fundoplication, based on low-certainty evidence.
SAGES strongly requires a complete fundoplication in every patient.
SAGES prohibits fundoplication.
SAGES says mesh eliminates recurrence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline conditionally suggests fundoplication; the supporting evidence is low certainty. It does not mandate a particular wrap or promise outcomes.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is an ABS MBS FPD eligibility distinction?

options.text: It is a focused practice designation exam, with separate eligibility/practice requirements; it is not a bariatric subspecialty board certification.
Completion of a one-year fellowship alone automatically grants board certification.
It is the same credential as Fellowship Council accreditation.
It is open to any learner without clinical experience.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS calls MBS a focused practice designation rather than a subspecialty certification and lists general surgery certification, experience, privileges and case requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: In the ABS MBS FPD content outline, which domains carry the largest stated weights?

options.text: Preop 30%, operations 25%, postoperative management 30%.
Obesity science 30%, pregnancy 30%, research 40%.
Surgery 100%.
All five domains exactly 20%.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Published outline lists obesity science 7.5%, preoperative 30%, operations 25%, postoperative 30%, special populations 7.5%.

practiceQuestions.stem: A publicly viewable ASMBS FELLOW Project recording is used in this independent curriculum. What credit can the learner infer?

options.text: No ASMBS certificate credit; ASMBS explicitly says public ASMBS/YouTube viewing does not satisfy its LMS requirements.
Automatic Fellowship Certificate credit.
Automatic CME credit from duration alone.
Board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASMBS explicitly distinguishes public video viewing from LMS completion for fellowship certificate/training requirements.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which MBSAQIP statement is accurate?

options.text: It is a voluntary center accreditation and quality-improvement program, not an individual board credential.
It is an individual surgeon board examination.
It grants a license.
It replaces surgical privileges.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACS describes MBSAQIP as center-focused accreditation, standards, site evaluation and quality measurement.

practiceQuestions.stem: How should the 2023 European Hernia Society midline incisional-hernia guideline be applied?

options.text: Within its adult midline incisional hernia scope; do not assume it directly resolves complex defects needing component separation.
As a universal rule for every abdominal wall defect.
Only for pediatric hernias.
As a bariatric candidacy rule.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline explicitly limits scope to adult midline incisional hernias expected to close without advanced adjunctive techniques such as component separation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient has weight recurrence after prior bariatric surgery. What is the best educational first step?

options.text: Map prior anatomy, course/outcomes, comorbidities, nutrition, behavioral/medical factors, symptoms and goals before comparing options.
Assume a single operative revision is indicated.
Use body weight alone to choose a revision.
Infer internal hernia from recurrence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS content outline includes assessment, complications, revisions and pharmacotherapy; weight recurrence merits a multidomain evaluation, not a diagnosis or operation based on one datum.

title: Endovascular and Cerebrovascular Surgery Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (independent self-study curriculum; not clinical training)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Designed for physicians, senior residents/fellows, or advanced health professionals studying neurovascular disease; not an eligibility pathway or procedural curriculum for unsupervised learners.

Recommended knowledge: neuroanatomy and cerebrovascular territories; vascular physiology; acute ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke assessment; basic CT/CTA, MR/MRA, and angiographic image interpretation; neurocritical-care principles; evidence-based practice and informed consent.

Learners should be able to distinguish diagnostic angiography from therapeutic intervention and to recognize that operative/endo cases require supervised accredited training, simulation, credentialing, and institutional privileges.
Board eligibility prerequisites are not course prerequisites and are determined only by the relevant institution and board.
objectives: Explain anterior/posterior circulation anatomy and localize vascular syndromes while accounting for variants and collateral pathways.
Interpret the role and limitations of CT/CTA, MR/MRA, perfusion imaging and catheter digital-subtraction angiography in a neurovascular diagnostic pathway.

Synthesize current evidence and multidisciplinary considerations for acute ischemic stroke, aneurysm, subarachnoid hemorrhage, AVM/AVF, carotid disease, moyamoya and selected other cerebrovascular disorders.
Compare open, endovascular and hybrid treatment rationales at a conceptual level without providing device instructions, case-volume claims, or procedural authorization.
Recognize how patient safety, complications, radiation stewardship, documentation, outcomes and evidence appraisal shape team decisions.
Map course coverage to published ACGME/CAST training requirements and the RFPD's published procedure categories without representing it as an official board blueprint.

assignment.title: Multidisciplinary neurovascular case conference and evidence dossier
assignment.instructions: Choose one fictional case or a source-linked public de-identified case dataset permitted for external viewing. Write a structured problem representation, identify the decision question, compare at least two plausible open/endovascular/hybrid pathways where relevant, state evidence and guideline currency, identify uncertainties and missing data, describe patient-centred discussion and team roles, and cite primary sources. Do not prescribe an individual patient's treatment or provide technical procedural steps. Do not submit clinical images, patient records, screenshots or copied clinical narratives.
assignment.completionThreshold: 80/100 on this local educational rubric only; not a validated exam predictor, certification or competence result.

mapping.institution: Brigham and Women's Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
mapping.name: BWH Endovascular and Cerebrovascular Fellowship; current page title: MGB Neurovascular Surgery – Combined Open and Endovascular Fellowship (Track B)
mapping.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes two years: year one diagnostic/interventional neuroendovascular training including aneurysm, stroke, AVM/AVF/tumour embolization, stents/angioplasty, head/neck work, spinal angiography/embolization and MMA embolization; year two open cerebrovascular surgery including Sylvian fissure dissection, clipping, AVM surgery, bypass, carotid surgery/endarterectomy, cavernous malformation and hematoma evacuation, with integrated endovascular decision-making. Entry requirements publicly state completion of a seven-year ACGME-approved neurosurgery residency and 200 diagnostic/interventional cerebral angiographic procedures as primary operator. The page's reported year-one 150-intervention count is not presented here as a full fellowship minimum or compared as if equivalent to ACGME's separate 250-procedure minimum. Page language emphasizes selecting among open, endovascular and hybrid options. Its institutional entry threshold and description do not establish board eligibility, accreditation, current available slots, or guaranteed case exposure.

topicGaps: Verified public free recordings total 15.7097 hours after this expansion, leaving an actual residual shortfall of 20.2903 hours against the 36-hour target. Original scripts, clip targets, assigned reading, case exercises and study-plan hours are not rendered media and are not counted.

There is no public board-exam blueprint/domain-weight table located for the CNS Endovascular RFPD; mapped competencies remain to published ACGME/CAST requirements and the joint board’s public eligibility/procedure categories, not a claim to predict its exam.

Long-form open teaching remains sparse for cranial dural AVF, spinal AVM, head/neck embolization, chronic subdural/MMA evidence, acute intra-procedural complications and outcomes. A newly sourced SDAVF article is a single-center retrospective cohort, not a guideline or randomized comparative study.

Open surgical procedures (Sylvian fissure dissection, clipping, bypass, AVM resection, carotid endarterectomy, cavernoma and hematoma surgery) cannot be learned to competence from these recordings or scripts; require supervised accredited training, simulation, credentialing and institutional privileges.

Public ACGME/CAST requirements, BWH/MGB institutional curriculum and CNS Endovascular RFPD pathways have different scope and eligibility rules. Do not transfer one pathway’s entry or case criteria to another.

Three University of Utah public grand-rounds records for pediatric neurovascular surgery, cerebral bypass and neurovascular imaging were viewable, but numeric runtime was not exposed in the fetched pages. They remain uncounted. ESMINT recordings catalog requires sign-in/membership and was excluded; no login was attempted.
Human clinician review has not been performed. The authored episodes are source-grounded education scripts only and require qualified clinical review before production or use in clinical training.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Neurological Surgery (ABNS)

medical.boardStatus: The institutional offering is a genuine physician fellowship, not a generic directory category, research-only postdoctoral appointment, or non-physician supplement. The public BWH/MGB page describes a two-year combined open and endovascular neurovascular surgery fellowship (Track B) for neurosurgery residency graduates with prior endovascular experience. CAST's current accredited-program directory lists Massachusetts General Brigham as a Neuroendovascular fellowship (NI1023, list updated December 2025); this listing is evidence of a CAST Neuroendovascular program at MGB, but the public record does not conclusively crosswalk the directory entry to every detail of BWH's combined Track B. ACGME separately recognizes Neuroendovascular Intervention as a 24-month subspecialty program; no public source retrieved in this review established that the specific BWH combined Track B is ACGME-accredited. The CNS Endovascular Recognition of Focused Practice Designation (RFPD) is an ABMS-approved joint focused-practice credential sponsored by ABNS, ABR, and ABPN, managed by ABNS, with a written exam; it is not a separate medical-specialty board certification. The applicable pathway depends on base-board certification and prerequisite training. No exam blueprint/domain weights were located in public sources; content mapping here is to published ACGME/CAST requirements and RFPD procedure categories, not a claim to reproduce or predict the exam.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: The BWH page states that its two-year offering is open to graduates of a seven-year ACGME-approved neurological surgery residency who have performed at least 200 catheter-based diagnostic and/or interventional cerebral angiographic procedures as primary operator. That institutional statement is not equivalent to ACGME/CAST accreditation status, ABNS board eligibility, or eligibility for the RFPD. ABNS base certification, current program rules, documented practice/cases, the appropriate credential pathway, and any future rule changes must be checked directly with the boards. ABR/ABPN pathways described on the joint RFPD page do not make those applicants eligible for the BWH Track B unless the institution confirms it. Do not use this curriculum to claim eligibility or credentials.

officialProgrammes.institution: Brigham and Women's Hospital (Mass General Brigham)
officialProgrammes.name: BWH Endovascular and Cerebrovascular Fellowship; current page title: MGB Neurovascular Surgery – Combined Open and Endovascular Fellowship (Track B)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes two years: year one diagnostic/interventional neuroendovascular training including aneurysm, stroke, AVM/AVF/tumour embolization, stents/angioplasty, head/neck work, spinal angiography/embolization and MMA embolization; year two open cerebrovascular surgery including Sylvian fissure dissection, clipping, AVM surgery, bypass, carotid surgery/endarterectomy, cavernous malformation and hematoma evacuation, with integrated endovascular decision-making. Entry requirements publicly state completion of a seven-year ACGME-approved neurosurgery residency and 200 diagnostic/interventional cerebral angiographic procedures as primary operator. The page's reported year-one 150-intervention count is not presented here as a full fellowship minimum or compared as if equivalent to ACGME's separate 250-procedure minimum. Page language emphasizes selecting among open, endovascular and hybrid options. Its institutional entry threshold and description do not establish board eligibility, accreditation, current available slots, or guaranteed case exposure.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This course packet follows the exact MED-X039 official programme variant from the discovery packet; the directory listing was a discovery lead, while the MGB/BWH programme page, ACGME, CAST and board pages were checked separately. The actual physician subspecialty is neuroendovascular/cerebrovascular surgery, and the named institutional variant is a combined open-plus-endovascular neurosurgical fellowship (Track B). It is not a separate board-certified specialty, not simply the generic 'neurology and neurosurgery' family, and not a research/non-physician track. No distinct board examination for 'open cerebrovascular surgery' was found. The joint CNS Endovascular RFPD has a separate written focused-practice exam, but it is a credential and not specialty-board certification. Research experience is part of the institutional fellowship, not a separate research fellowship variant. No Johns Hopkins clinical track was added because the assigned item packet names only the BWH/MGB variant; CAST's MGB directory entry is preserved as an accreditation-source variant/caveat, not a second institutional offering.

topicGaps: Verified public free recordings total 15.7097 hours after this expansion, leaving an actual residual shortfall of 20.2903 hours against the 36-hour target. Original scripts, clip targets, assigned reading, case exercises and study-plan hours are not rendered media and are not counted.

There is no public board-exam blueprint/domain-weight table located for the CNS Endovascular RFPD; mapped competencies remain to published ACGME/CAST requirements and the joint board’s public eligibility/procedure categories, not a claim to predict its exam.

Long-form open teaching remains sparse for cranial dural AVF, spinal AVM, head/neck embolization, chronic subdural/MMA evidence, acute intra-procedural complications and outcomes. A newly sourced SDAVF article is a single-center retrospective cohort, not a guideline or randomized comparative study.

Open surgical procedures (Sylvian fissure dissection, clipping, bypass, AVM resection, carotid endarterectomy, cavernoma and hematoma surgery) cannot be learned to competence from these recordings or scripts; require supervised accredited training, simulation, credentialing and institutional privileges.

Public ACGME/CAST requirements, BWH/MGB institutional curriculum and CNS Endovascular RFPD pathways have different scope and eligibility rules. Do not transfer one pathway’s entry or case criteria to another.

Three University of Utah public grand-rounds records for pediatric neurovascular surgery, cerebral bypass and neurovascular imaging were viewable, but numeric runtime was not exposed in the fetched pages. They remain uncounted. ESMINT recordings catalog requires sign-in/membership and was excluded; no login was attempted.
Human clinician review has not been performed. The authored episodes are source-grounded education scripts only and require qualified clinical review before production or use in clinical training.

assignment.title: Capstone — source-annotated fictional nuclear cardiology conference
assignment.instructions: Using one cited ASNC published case link or an explicitly fictional text-only vignette, submit (1) the clinical question and modality limits, (2) acquisition/QC checklist, (3) integrated perfusion/function/MBF/calcification reasoning if reported, (4) differential and uncertainty, (5) concise structured report draft for educational discussion, (6) source list and rights check. Do not copy images, identifiable data, proprietary questions, or write real-patient management advice. All case material submitted by the learner must be de-identified and lawfully used.

rubric.standard: Claims mapped to authoritative current source; separates educational inference from published rule.
Explicitly checks acquisition, registration/motion/bolus and names unresolved limitations.
Integrates available perfusion, function, MBF/MBFR and anatomy/calcium without relying on a single metric.
No unsupported diagnosis/treatment; includes differential and supervised escalation boundary.
Clear structured report, fictional or approved source case, no image/data rehosting.

assignment.passingRule: Course design rubric only; not validated and not a substitute for clinical assessment or board readiness.
