unitMap.text: Training scope, readiness, and governance
coveredTopics: Institutional fellowship listing; accreditation and credential boundaries; informed limitations.

unitMap.text: Cardiac tracer principles and study design
coveredTopics: Tracer uptake/extraction; rest-stress design; exercise/pharmacologic stress as study context; dose and exposure concepts; protocol dependence.

unitMap.text: Instrumentation, SPECT/PET physics, and image reconstruction
coveredTopics: Gamma-camera and PET fundamentals; ECG gating; CT attenuation correction; registration; motion, scatter, attenuation, resolution, normalization, reconstruction and QC.

unitMap.text: Patient selection, stress testing, safety, and appropriateness
coveredTopics: Exercise vs pharmacologic stress; contraindications and adverse-event readiness; radiation protection; patient preparation; appropriateness of SPECT/PET/CT alternatives.

unitMap.text: SPECT MPI acquisition, quality review, and standard reading sequence
coveredTopics: Acquisition design; raw data; attenuation correction; prone/upright comparison; gating; 17-segment model; summed scores as context.

unitMap.text: MPI interpretation, stress response, and risk communication
coveredTopics: Reversible/fixed defects; extent/severity; gated function; transient dilation; calcium context; probability/risk communication and report conventions.

unitMap.text: Cardiac PET perfusion and quantitative MBF/MBFR
coveredTopics: Dynamic imaging/input function; model/software; motion, IV, registration, bolus errors; regional/global MBFR; vasodilator response; cautious interpretation.

unitMap.text: PET/SPECT discordance, multivessel disease, and microvascular dysfunction
coveredTopics: Balanced ischemia; CMD/INOCA; flow reserve; calcium/CCTA context; discordant perfusion and MBF; test limitations.

unitMap.text: Cardiac amyloidosis scintigraphy and multimodality integration
coveredTopics: PYP/DPD/HMDP; planar/SPECT; visual grades and H/CL caveats; AL exclusion using serum free light chains and serum/urine immunofixation; echo/CMR integration.

unitMap.text: Inflammation, viability, innervation, and molecular cardiac imaging
coveredTopics: FDG inflammation preparation; sarcoidosis imaging; viability; sympathetic innervation; emerging molecular imaging; multimodality correlation.

unitMap.text: Radiation protection, quality systems, and reporting
coveredTopics: Radiation-safety principles; equipment QA; error reporting; structured report; dose stewardship; communication and quality improvement.

unitMap.text: Evidence synthesis, board blueprint, and integrated review
coveredTopics: CBNC knowledge areas: tests; test performance/instrumentation/protocols/processing; safe radionuclide use; QC; interpretation/appropriate use; evidence appraisal and integrated practice.

topicGaps: Observed, public full-watch-page duration totals are 9.8139 hours across 9 unique recordings. The 36-hour floor remains short by 26.1861 hours; planned minutes and authored scripts are not rendered hours.
ASNC lists 28-module Cardiac PET Curriculum and 16-module PET Perfusion Essentials OnDemand courses; free public access and module durations were not verified, so neither package is counted.

No fully open, duration-verified public lecture set was located for PYP/amyloid scintigraphy or the whole CBNC domain set. Public practice documents and the original scripts supplement but do not replace supervised image review.

FDG applications for viability, inflammation/sarcoidosis and infection require question-specific current protocols. A public ASNC FDG-viability transcript was accessible but its player runtime was not observed; detailed preparation and interpretation remain intentionally under-sourced here.
Public lectures on SPECT, stress protocols, PET QC and MBF are concentrated in older recordings (2019–2022); use current society guidance and local protocols for date-sensitive practice.
Public MGH materials do not disclose a programme-specific rotation calendar, case volumes, didactic lecture set, full fellowship duration, or a verified ACGME accreditation statement.
The course cannot provide required case logs, preceptor attestations, supervised Level 2 hours, hands-on laboratory/radiation-safety work, clinical privileges or examination eligibility.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardStatus.status: CBNC is a distinct certification exam/credential. The source describes a qualified specialty exam for CBNC certification/diplomate status. CBNC is not evidence that this particular institutional fellowship is a separate ACGME-accredited fellowship or that it confers ABMS board certification. Current 2026 US eligibility requires documented Level 2 training/experience (minimum 700 hours including 80 hours classroom/lab), qualifying current physician license and current certification in Cardiology, an ABIM cardiology subspecialty, Nuclear Medicine or Radiology from an ABMS-member or AOA board, plus required documentation. Verify live criteria before application.

topicGaps: Observed, public full-watch-page duration totals are 9.8139 hours across 9 unique recordings. The 36-hour floor remains short by 26.1861 hours; planned minutes and authored scripts are not rendered hours.
ASNC lists 28-module Cardiac PET Curriculum and 16-module PET Perfusion Essentials OnDemand courses; free public access and module durations were not verified, so neither package is counted.

No fully open, duration-verified public lecture set was located for PYP/amyloid scintigraphy or the whole CBNC domain set. Public practice documents and the original scripts supplement but do not replace supervised image review.

FDG applications for viability, inflammation/sarcoidosis and infection require question-specific current protocols. A public ASNC FDG-viability transcript was accessible but its player runtime was not observed; detailed preparation and interpretation remain intentionally under-sourced here.
Public lectures on SPECT, stress protocols, PET QC and MBF are concentrated in older recordings (2019–2022); use current society guidance and local protocols for date-sensitive practice.
Public MGH materials do not disclose a programme-specific rotation calendar, case volumes, didactic lecture set, full fellowship duration, or a verified ACGME accreditation statement.
The course cannot provide required case logs, preceptor attestations, supervised Level 2 hours, hands-on laboratory/radiation-safety work, clinical privileges or examination eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner compares MGH’s public nuclear cardiology fellowship description with ACGME CVD requirements. Which statement is supported?

options.text: The MGH page states applicants must first complete cardiovascular disease fellowship and describes SPECT, PET/CT, molecular imaging, multimodality interpretation, radiation safety and QA.
The MGH fellowship is automatically an ABMS board.
Self-study substitutes for its prerequisite.
The page reports a guaranteed CBNC pass rate.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The institutional page explicitly lists completed cardiovascular disease fellowship and the stated imaging/curriculum elements; it does not state board award or equivalence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Under the 2026 ACGME CVD requirements, what specific nuclear-cardiology interpretation minimum is listed for CVD fellows?

options.text: 100 radionuclide studies, including SPECT MPI and ventriculograms.
300 cardiac PET cases.
700 nuclear studies.
No nuclear competence is required.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2026 requirements list competence and minimum interpretation of 100 radionuclide studies, including SPECT MPI and ventriculograms; this is a CVD programme requirement, not a claim of MGH fellowship volume.

practiceQuestions.stem: A US physician asks whether completing this online course makes them eligible for CBNC. Best answer?

options.text: Yes, because video hours replace supervised hours.

No; 2026 criteria include documented Level 2 training/experience, 700 hours including 80 hours classroom/laboratory, current unrestricted U.S. license, and qualifying board certification, among other criteria.
Yes, if they read the PYP PDF.
Eligibility is automatic after any cardiology fellowship.

practiceQuestions.rationale: APCA lists multiple eligibility conditions including training/experience, licensure, and board certification. Independent online education cannot document supervised cases, authorized-user training, or licensing.

practiceQuestions.stem: A dynamic cardiac PET sequence begins after the tracer bolus has passed the blood pool. Which concern is most relevant?

options.text: The input function may be missed and MBF can be overestimated.
The PYP visual grade is automatically positive.
Only relative perfusion is affected; MBF is always valid.
The attenuation correction is unnecessary.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC advises starting acquisition before tracer injection so the input function is captured; starting too late can lead to overestimated MBF.

practiceQuestions.stem: A PET MBFR is low but absolute stress MBF is preserved; resting heart rate and blood pressure are elevated. What is the most careful interpretation?

options.text: A low ratio alone proves obstructive multivessel CAD.
Elevated resting MBF may contribute; interpret stress and rest values, rate-pressure context, QC, perfusion, and calcium rather than treating MBFR alone as decisive.
The study is normal by definition.
Repeat the study immediately using an unsupervised protocol.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC describes cases in which elevated resting MBF with normal stress MBF can lower MBFR and notes patient context and QC matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner reviews a published PET MBF case with normal relative perfusion, low global MBFR, and elevated coronary calcium. What is the safest learning conclusion?

options.text: Normal relative perfusion excludes clinically important disease.
Use the combined pattern to recognize discordance and increased concern, but do not infer a specific diagnosis or treatment without the full supervised clinical context.
High calcium means PYP scan is positive.
MBFR is irrelevant whenever perfusion is normal.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC case compendium demonstrates that quantitative MBF and calcium can add information beyond perfusion; a published case is an educational example, not a definitive individual patient plan.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional suspected cardiac ATTR case, planar PYP appears grade 2 but SPECT shows prominent blood-pool activity without clear myocardial localization. Which principle is correct?

options.text: Diagnose ATTR based on planar grade alone.
Use SPECT to distinguish blood pool from myocardial uptake; do not diagnose solely from H/CL, and evaluate AL with serum free light chains plus serum/urine immunofixation.
Ignore monoclonal protein testing if uptake is present.
All positive planar studies equal ATTR.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASNC recommends SPECT localization and emphasizes AL can show uptake; monoclonal protein exclusion is required. H/CL alone is not sufficient.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which finding is the best reason to withhold a quantitative MBF result from a report draft for qualified review?

options.text: Unresolved misregistration, motion, poor bolus or input-function capture.
The scan contains both rest and stress values.
The report is structured.
A 17-segment model was used.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These are listed ASNC QC failure types that can compromise MBF; the responsible service must assess adequacy before use.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most defensible statement about ASNC OnDemand Cardiac PET Curricula?

options.text: All 28 modules are verified free public videos of known runtime.

ASNC describes a 28-module curriculum and a 16-module Perfusion Essentials OnDemand course, but their page does not establish public free access or runtimes; do not count them as open verified video hours.
They are automatically part of MGH curriculum.
They are board-exam questions.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The public resource center links curricula but notes OnDemand education; access and module runtimes were not verified as publicly free. They are excluded from the video ledger.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a physician training program, ACGME accreditation, and CBNC credentialing?

options.text: Any official page called fellowship proves ACGME accreditation and ABMS board eligibility.

The MGH page establishes an institutional advanced physician fellowship listing; it does not publish accreditation status. ACGME requirements define accredited CVD training; CBNC is a separate specialty certification exam with its own eligibility requirements.
CBNC is the ACGME.
A fellowship cannot be clinical training.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The available official sources support a listed physician fellowship, CVD ACGME requirement context, and separate CBNC certification, but not a claim that this track itself is ACGME accredited or confers certification.

title: Cardio-Oncology and Amyloid Heart Disease Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (official programme listing; MGB categorizes it as non-GME)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.level: Advanced post-cardiology-fellowship physician self-study; not an entry-level medical or clinical competency programme.
knowledge: Cardiovascular physiology, heart failure, ischemic disease, arrhythmias, ECG and echocardiography fundamentals
Cancer biology, common systemic therapy classes and hematologic malignancy terminology at introductory level
Reading clinical literature, risk assessment and multidisciplinary shared decision-making
prerequisites.boundary: Only the institutional programme sets trainee eligibility. Its public page requires completion of an ACGME-equivalent three-year general cardiology fellowship. These self-study materials are not an application or eligibility pathway.

objectives: Integrate cancer-treatment intent, prognosis and patient priorities with cardiovascular risks without reflexively delaying effective cancer care.
Construct a baseline, on-treatment and survivorship cardiovascular assessment using history, examination, ECG, biomarkers and risk-appropriate imaging.

Recognize and reason through cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, ischemia/vasospasm, hypertension, arrhythmia/QT prolongation, thrombosis, bleeding, pericardial and radiation-associated disease linked to cancer or treatment.
Distinguish AL from ATTR cardiac amyloidosis and apply a safe monoclonal-protein-first diagnostic pathway, interpreting echo, CMR and bone-avid tracer imaging in context.
Explain multidisciplinary management principles and evidence/uncertainty for AL-directed therapy, ATTR therapies, heart failure, arrhythmia, transplant and survivorship care.
Communicate uncertainty and escalation needs, use authentic case literature lawfully, and identify when a clinical decision requires specialist assessment.

topicGaps: Regimen-specific baseline risk, newer therapies and current surveillance recommendations remain incompletely represented by public recordings; a 2020 research talk is a dated supplement, not a current guideline.

Quantitative echo/GLS quality control, cross-platform reproducibility, biomarkers and modality artifacts need more depth; the 2023 Utah echo talk adds a relevant topic but does not establish complete skill coverage.
Decision-making under limited cardio-oncology trial evidence needs case-based teaching; the 2020 cohorts/trials recording is a dated supplement, not a validated syllabus.
Urgent ICI myocarditis evaluation, competing ACS/infection/demand causes, and myositis/myasthenia overlap remain insufficiently taught by verified recordings.
Cancer-associated thrombosis, bleeding, QT/drug interactions and treatment-related vascular complications remain gaps.
Radiation-associated disease, cumulative exposure, peri-transplant risk and survivorship are not adequately covered by the verified new recordings.
AL urgency, hematology interface, monoclonal testing and tissue typing remain incompletely covered; dated amyloid talks do not replace current pathway teaching.
ATTR genetics and rapidly changing therapeutic labels require current FDA-label review; historical Utah talks are not current treatment authorities.
PYP/DPD/HMDP acquisition, SPECT localization, blood pool and false-positive/false-negative patterns need supervised technical teaching; public videos do not replace local protocol.
Amyloid HF, arrhythmia, transplant, advanced disease, supportive care and multidisciplinary case reasoning remain insufficiently covered.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent curriculum confers no board eligibility. ABIM cardiovascular disease certification requires the applicable prior internal medicine certification, eligible accredited cardiovascular fellowship training, clinical competence and licensure; completion of this listed non-GME fellowship alone does not satisfy those criteria. Verify current rules with the certifying body.

There is no authoritative published cardio-oncology or amyloid board exam blueprint identified for this fellowship. ABIM cardiovascular disease and IC-OS knowledge certification are separate routes with distinct prerequisites; this curriculum is not eligibility evidence.

topicGaps: Regimen-specific baseline risk, newer therapies and current surveillance recommendations remain incompletely represented by public recordings; a 2020 research talk is a dated supplement, not a current guideline.

Quantitative echo/GLS quality control, cross-platform reproducibility, biomarkers and modality artifacts need more depth; the 2023 Utah echo talk adds a relevant topic but does not establish complete skill coverage.
Decision-making under limited cardio-oncology trial evidence needs case-based teaching; the 2020 cohorts/trials recording is a dated supplement, not a validated syllabus.
Urgent ICI myocarditis evaluation, competing ACS/infection/demand causes, and myositis/myasthenia overlap remain insufficiently taught by verified recordings.
Cancer-associated thrombosis, bleeding, QT/drug interactions and treatment-related vascular complications remain gaps.
Radiation-associated disease, cumulative exposure, peri-transplant risk and survivorship are not adequately covered by the verified new recordings.
AL urgency, hematology interface, monoclonal testing and tissue typing remain incompletely covered; dated amyloid talks do not replace current pathway teaching.
ATTR genetics and rapidly changing therapeutic labels require current FDA-label review; historical Utah talks are not current treatment authorities.
PYP/DPD/HMDP acquisition, SPECT localization, blood pool and false-positive/false-negative patterns need supervised technical teaching; public videos do not replace local protocol.
Amyloid HF, arrhythmia, transplant, advanced disease, supportive care and multidisciplinary case reasoning remain insufficiently covered.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient on cancer therapy has a modest change in global longitudinal strain from baseline but no new symptoms. Which is the best next reasoning step?

options.text: Declare definite cardiotoxicity from GLS alone and stop all cancer therapy.
Review image quality and comparable serial studies, clinical context and biomarkers, then discuss risk-appropriate management with oncology and cardiology.
Ignore GLS because only symptoms matter.
Diagnose myocarditis without further assessment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A single imaging metric needs technical and clinical context. ESC guidance supports structured, risk-based surveillance and collaborative decisions that balance CV risk and cancer-treatment benefit; neither automatic cessation nor dismissal is justified.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has suspected cardiac amyloidosis and a positive technetium-PYP scan. Serum immunofixation shows a monoclonal protein. What conclusion is most appropriate?

options.text: The scan alone proves ATTR cardiomyopathy.
AL has been excluded because tracer uptake is present.
Do not diagnose ATTR noninvasively from the scan alone; pursue specialist assessment and tissue typing as indicated because AL remains possible.
Use serum protein electrophoresis alone to determine subtype.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A monoclonal screen must be interpreted before a nonbiopsy ATTR pathway. A positive component requires evaluation for AL and potentially involved-organ biopsy with amyloid typing; monoclonal gammopathy may coexist with ATTR.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which test set is the appropriate initial monoclonal-protein screen in suspected cardiac amyloidosis?

options.text: Serum protein electrophoresis only.
Serum free light chains plus serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis.
Urine dipstick only.
PYP scan alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACC consensus identifies all three tests—serum free light chains, serum immunofixation and urine immunofixation—as the initial screen. Routine electrophoresis alone is insufficient to rule out a monoclonal protein.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional case has negative fat-pad biopsy but persistent clinical concern for cardiac amyloid. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Amyloidosis is excluded.
ATTR is proven.
A negative fat-pad biopsy does not exclude AL or ATTR; assess the involved organ and full diagnostic pathway.
Repeat PYP until positive.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACC consensus explicitly notes that a negative fat-pad biopsy does not rule out AL or ATTR. Consider involved-organ biopsy when clinically indicated and integrate laboratory/imaging evidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient receiving an immune checkpoint inhibitor develops chest discomfort, new ECG changes and troponin elevation. Which approach is safest?

options.text: Assume benign demand injury and wait for routine follow-up.
Treat possible ICI myocarditis as an urgent differential; escalate multidisciplinary assessment and investigate competing diagnoses promptly.
Use a normal ejection fraction to exclude myocarditis.
Diagnose coronary vasospasm without evaluation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ICI myocarditis can be serious and requires urgent assessment; normal LVEF does not exclude it. ESC guidance addresses clinical evaluation and management, while differential includes ACS and other causes of myocardial injury.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has unexplained LV wall thickening and low ECG voltage. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: This combination is required and pathognomonic for cardiac amyloidosis.
It is a supportive clue, but it occurs in a minority and is neither required nor independently diagnostic.
It rules out hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
It establishes ATTR rather than AL.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACC consensus notes that low voltage with hypertrophy is present in only about 30% of amyloid patients; phenotype clues increase suspicion but do not type amyloid or establish diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description best distinguishes the listed MGB cardio-oncology/amyloid fellowship from the ABIM cardiovascular disease pathway?

options.text: MGB's page labels its one-year fellowship Non-GME; the ABIM cardiovascular disease exam has separate accredited-training and eligibility requirements.
Completion automatically grants ABIM cardiology certification.
Cardio-oncology is an ABIM subspecialty exam listed on the cardiovascular certification page.
The optional research year grants board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The MGB official page categorizes the fellowship as Non-GME. ABIM cardiovascular disease certification has formal prerequisites including specified accredited training; no cardio-oncology exam appears in the reviewed ABIM subspecialty list.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with suspected ATTR cardiomyopathy has a diagnostic pathway supporting ATTR. What additional step distinguishes hereditary from wild-type ATTR?

options.text: No additional test is needed; cardiac imaging distinguishes the genotype.
TTR genetic testing with appropriate counseling.
Serum protein electrophoresis alone.
Repeat echocardiography only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACC consensus recommends genetic testing to distinguish ATTRwt from ATTRv after ATTR-CM is established; counseling and implications for family are important.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about cardio-oncology certification is supported by reviewed official sources?

options.text: IC-OS offers a Cardio-Oncology Knowledge Certification with its own stated requirements; it is a society credential, not ABIM/ABMS board certification.
The MGB fellowship automatically waives all IC-OS requirements.
IC-OS certification is an ABIM subspecialty certificate.
An online course alone is documented to confer eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: IC-OS publishes a separate society examination and requires defined membership, clinical training/experience and references. The credential is not represented as ABMS board certification, and course completion here does not confer eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with cardiac amyloidosis and atrial fibrillation is being considered for cardioversion. Which teaching point is supported by the ACC consensus?

options.text: Use CHA2DS2-VASc alone to decide whether anticoagulation is ever indicated.
Amyloidosis carries intracardiac thrombus concern; consensus recommends anticoagulation for AF regardless of CHA2DS2-VASc and TEE before cardioversion regardless of anticoagulation status.
A normal ECG excludes atrial thrombus.
Cardioversion requires no imaging if anticoagulated.

practiceQuestions.rationale: This reflects the 2023 ACC consensus summary. Individual decisions require clinician assessment of bleeding risk and current guidance; the learning point is not an order for any real person.

unitMap.text: Inheritance, haplotypes, population and sensitization

coveredTopics: Serologic typing; amplification-based assays; sequence-based typing; NGS; ambiguity; resolution; confirmatory typing.

unitMap.text: Anti-HLA antibody assays and interpretation

unitMap.text: Other transplant and extended H&I applications
coveredTopics: HCT; solid organs; tissue; transfusion; chimerism; non-classical loci; immune-function applications.

unitMap.text: Quality systems, validation and proficiency testing
coveredTopics: Preanalytic identity; validation; controls; reagent/instrument; competency; PT; complaints; audit; corrective action; confidentiality.

unitMap.text: Result communication, informatics and data stewardship
coveredTopics: Result reporting; discrepancies; critical results; database versioning; audit trail; privacy; donor-recipient data; informatics.

unitMap.text: Professional judgment, ethics and integrated review

officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The official page displays this fellowship title and a contact for William Lane, MD, PhD. It publishes no eligibility, rotations, curriculum, duration, accreditation status or exam outcomes; do not infer these from the title or contact.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The supplied discovery packet places this item in the official MGB GME directory under Medicine and calls it a Clinical physician fellowship; the generic MGB directory search page itself does not expose the specific result in stateless extraction. The direct BWH page verifies the exact offering title/contact only. Public evidence reviewed does not establish whether this is a physician-only clinical fellowship, a laboratory-director trainee pathway open to multiple degree backgrounds, a combined programme, a research fellowship, or another generic directory category. It is not a combined programme based on evidence found, but absence of published detail is not proof. Preserve the exact institutional variant and do not silently recategorize. The ASHI approved fellowship list fetched did not name BWH; this is not proof the programme is unapproved because the list may be incomplete/dated. ACGME Pathology program list does not list Histocompatibility and Immunogenetics as a program/subspecialty.
sourceCaveats: Institution page is sparse; training eligibility, accreditation, curriculum, fellow identity and outcomes remain unverified.
ACHI exam is an individual professional laboratory credential route, not a separate physician specialty board; the BWH page does not specify relationship to it.
The ASHI Approved Fellowship Programs PDF retrieved did not list BWH, but no authoritative statement was found that this directory is exhaustive/current for every programme.
ASHI 2025 Standards PDF says CMS approved January 27, 2026; its own applicability and later updates must be checked before operational use.
The retrieved OPTN policies are effective October 1, 2026. A webpage or policy can change; recheck version/date before clinical or compliance use.
HRSA/OPTN recommended histocompatibility guidelines are explicitly recommendations and are historically dated; not presented as current binding policy.

Human clinical review is not performed. This independent educational course grants no affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, laboratory directorship, procedure competence, certification or guarantee of passing.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best distinguishes ASHI accreditation and ACHI certification?

options.text: ASHI accredits laboratories; ACHI issues individual professional credentials.
ASHI issues a physician subspecialty certificate; ACHI accredits hospitals.
Both are interchangeable institution accreditors.
ACHI accreditation alone licenses a person to practice medicine.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASHI standards address accredited laboratory requirements; ACHI describes individual director credentials and examination pathways. They are not equivalent, and neither statement grants medical licensure.

practiceQuestions.stem: A laboratory result assigns a haplotype partly from population frequencies. Which reporting principle is most accurate?

options.text: Report it as proven genotype because the frequency is high.
Clearly identify that phase was inferred from population frequencies and cite the source; family segregation or other evidence may be needed for proof.
Do not report any haplotype under any circumstances.
Treat two identical serologic antigens as definitive allele-level proof.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASHI standards require clarity when haplotypes are assigned from population frequencies and note the limits of proven identity; frequency inference is not direct phasing evidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: A donor-recipient mismatch inquiry involves unrelated allogeneic HCT. What is a defensible general teaching point from NMDP/CIBMTR guidance?

options.text: Low-resolution matching is always equivalent to allele-level matching.
High-resolution allele-level matching at key loci and DPB1 permissiveness may matter, within the patient, donor, disease and transplant context.
A DPB1 mismatch alone determines that transplant cannot proceed.
Solid-organ MFI cutoffs decide HCT donor selection.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The open-access NMDP/CIBMTR synthesis emphasizes high-resolution HLA matching and DPB1 considerations; it does not authorize a universal decision rule, and solid-organ MFI thresholds should not be imported.

practiceQuestions.stem: A single-antigen bead assay yields a high MFI. What conclusion is justified from MFI alone?

options.text: A universal antibody concentration and fixed clinical risk.
The assay signal is elevated, but its interpretation depends on assay characteristics, specificity, history and correlation; no universal clinical cutoff follows from MFI alone.
A positive physical crossmatch is guaranteed.
The antibody is necessarily complement-binding.

practiceQuestions.rationale: MFI is a semiquantitative assay signal rather than a standardized concentration; current case interpretation integrates pattern, testing conditions, donor typing, history, controls and center/lab practice. ASHI standards govern methods and antibody identification.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is a correct role distinction for a virtual crossmatch?

options.text: A virtual crossmatch is itself a cell-based laboratory test.
It is an interpretive comparison of available donor HLA information with recipient antibody data and context; it does not always replace a physical crossmatch.
A negative VXM proves absence of all anti-HLA antibodies.
It removes the need to consider sample recency or sensitizing events.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASHI consultation examples show VXM as a clinical-laboratory interpretation with limits; recent testing and intervening sensitization matter, and the proper physical-test strategy is governed by protocol and clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: An unexpected positive flow crossmatch occurs without an identified donor-specific HLA antibody. Which reasoning is safest?

options.text: Declare an HLA incompatibility as certain.
Consider auto-reactivity or other non-HLA interference, verify controls and result context, and follow laboratory procedures for investigation/escalation.
Ignore the crossmatch because antibody testing is negative.
Report a negative crossmatch by default.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASHI’s examples specifically illustrate auto-reactivity and unexplained reactivity as interpretive issues. The laboratory must use its validated procedures and clinical escalation; no educational item directs a real transplant decision.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the 2025 ASHI Standards is supported by the document?

options.text: They cover only HLA allele nomenclature.
They include general quality systems, method-specific standards, applications, post-analytic systems and personnel.
They are an ACGME physician curriculum.
They replace OPTN policy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The retrieved table of contents includes accreditation, proficiency testing, quality systems, analytic/application-specific methods, post-analytic systems and personnel. They are not an ACGME curriculum or a replacement for current OPTN policy.

practiceQuestions.stem: A trainee needs to check current U.S. OPTN requirements for H&I rather than rely on an older consensus PDF. What should be prioritized?

options.text: Older HRSA recommended guidelines as binding policy.
The OPTN policies/bylaws currently effective, particularly Policy 4 Histocompatibility, plus applicable laboratory standards.
A commercial vendor webinar.
An obsolete public comment draft.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The older OPTN/UNOS guideline expressly calls itself recommendations, not standards, and reflects historical policy. The current OPTN policy set lists Policy 4 Histocompatibility; confirm effective dates.

practiceQuestions.stem: The official BWH page for the item lists a fellowship title and a contact, but no eligibility requirements. Which conclusion is warranted?

options.text: It proves applicants must be board-certified physicians.
It proves this is a non-physician PhD fellowship.
The institutional listing is verified, but eligibility, physician-only status, curriculum and accreditation remain unverified from the public page.
It proves the candidate is eligible for a separate ABMS exam.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The retrieved institutional page gives a fellowship title and a contact route only. It does not state eligibility, curriculum or accreditation, so those matters should remain explicitly unresolved.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is accurate about the accessible ASHI virtual crossmatch examples?

options.text: They are a validated board examination and patient dataset licensed for rehosting.
They are publicly linked educational consultation examples; free viewing does not grant permission to rehost, and they should not be treated as universal decision thresholds.
They replace laboratory protocols.
They prove MFI categories are universal clinical thresholds.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2024 ASHI Directors Affairs Committee PDF is an educational example resource. Copyright/permissions are not granted for copying, and its own examples are not universal decision rules or a substitute for local validated procedures.

topicGaps: The current verified ledger is only 3.7828 of the 36 target hours (3.7828 hours total: 2.7425 specialty + 1.0403 cross-cutting RV foundation); 32.2172 hours remain. Scripted episodes and minute-targeted production plans are not recordings and contribute zero verified media hours.

Insufficient runtime-verified lectures remain for transplant referral/candidate evaluation depth; U.S. OPTN Policy 6 and pediatric allocation workflow; donor-offer and exception reasoning; temporary MCS/ECMO and procedural/safety boundaries; transplant operative planning; perioperative primary graft dysfunction; lung transplant procurement/implantation; rejection/immunosuppression/infection; long-term graft/device outcomes and quality methods.

The new recordings add conceptual LVAD selection/strategy, broad RV physiology with LVAD context, LVAD quality-of-life/ethics, and heart-preservation/perfusion discussion. They do not provide full device-management, procedural, policy-workshop, or rejection curricula.

The public BWH listing still does not publish programme curriculum, duration, entry eligibility, ACGME accreditation or case volume. A transplant/MCS-specific ABTS board exam was not identified in the reviewed ABTS materials; map only to parent thoracic-surgery learning domains, not an invented certificate.

Measured public surgical case demonstrations V05/V06/V07 remain excluded as procedures rather than didactic lectures; V06/V07 are the same canonical video. Unknown runtimes for V01–V04 and V08 remain uncounted.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Exact institutional variant is preserved from the MGB official listing. The public page classifies a Fellowship in Surgery. It is not a combined residency, generic directory label only, or research/non-physician supplement in the packet; however, its clinical-physician entry prerequisites and accreditation are not documented on the page. No evidence reviewed establishes the particular offering as ACGME-accredited. The separate ACGME independent thoracic surgery requirements are used only as a learning-domain reference, not as proof of this programme’s accreditation. No Johns Hopkins variant for this exact track is established in the supplied official packet.
sourceCaveats: BWH public programme page is terse. Accreditation, prerequisite training, duration, rotations, operative volumes and official curriculum are not verified.
ACGME 2026 independent thoracic surgery standards are referenced as authoritative GME context only, not assigned to BWH without evidence or treated as a board blueprint.

ABTS pathway identifies primary thoracic certification; the ABTS site separately lists congenital subspecialty certification. No transplant/MCS board exam was located in the reviewed ABTS content. The negative search is bounded to the materials reviewed.

topicGaps: The current verified ledger is only 3.7828 of the 36 target hours (3.7828 hours total: 2.7425 specialty + 1.0403 cross-cutting RV foundation); 32.2172 hours remain. Scripted episodes and minute-targeted production plans are not recordings and contribute zero verified media hours.

Insufficient runtime-verified lectures remain for transplant referral/candidate evaluation depth; U.S. OPTN Policy 6 and pediatric allocation workflow; donor-offer and exception reasoning; temporary MCS/ECMO and procedural/safety boundaries; transplant operative planning; perioperative primary graft dysfunction; lung transplant procurement/implantation; rejection/immunosuppression/infection; long-term graft/device outcomes and quality methods.

The new recordings add conceptual LVAD selection/strategy, broad RV physiology with LVAD context, LVAD quality-of-life/ethics, and heart-preservation/perfusion discussion. They do not provide full device-management, procedural, policy-workshop, or rejection curricula.

The public BWH listing still does not publish programme curriculum, duration, entry eligibility, ACGME accreditation or case volume. A transplant/MCS-specific ABTS board exam was not identified in the reviewed ABTS materials; map only to parent thoracic-surgery learning domains, not an invented certificate.

Measured public surgical case demonstrations V05/V06/V07 remain excluded as procedures rather than didactic lectures; V06/V07 are the same canonical video. Unknown runtimes for V01–V04 and V08 remain uncounted.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best characterizes this BWH listing?

options.text: It proves ACGME accreditation and ABTS eligibility.
It is an official institution directory listing of a Fellowship in Surgery, but the page does not state accreditation, length, eligibility or curriculum.
It is a research-only postdoctoral supplement.
It establishes a separate MCS board.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The MGB page labels it Fellowship and Surgery and gives a contact, but publishes no programme curriculum, accreditation or board status. Do not infer eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: Does completion of this fellowship alone establish ABTS primary certification?

options.text: Yes; all MCS fellows receive ABTS primary certification.
No; ABTS primary certification has specified eligible training pathways, examinations and licensure requirements; the directory listing alone proves none.
Yes, if the learner watched 36 hours.
Only if an ISHLT exam is passed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS pathway criteria are distinct from a fellowship listing and require an approved pathway plus examination and unrestricted U.S. license.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is supported about a separate board exam for transplant/MCS?

options.text: ABTS lists a dedicated MCS exam.
The reviewed ABTS materials identify primary thoracic certification and a separate congenital subspecialty; no transplant/MCS-specific board exam was identified.
ISHLT awards ABTS certification.
All institutional fellowship offerings are board exams.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABTS lists a distinct congenital cardiac surgery certificate/exam; reviewed pathways provide no comparable transplant/MCS board. This negative search is scoped to reviewed materials.

practiceQuestions.stem: What source governs U.S. transplant-member heart-status rules?

options.text: A historical review article only.
The current OPTN Policy 6, checked for effective date and full applicable criteria.
A video lecture.
This course guide.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The OPTN current policies updated 2026-10-01 include Policy 6. Historical articles cannot replace current rules.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the safest interpretation of an LVAD right-heart-failure risk score?

options.text: A low score guarantees no RHF.
It is an adjunct; definitions vary and external validation of several tools has been limited.
It replaces multidisciplinary assessment.
It is identical to an OPTN allocation status.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The open review describes heterogeneous RHF definitions and limited external validation; do not turn a model estimate into certainty.

practiceQuestions.stem: How should this curriculum use the FDA-hosted HeartMate 3 IFU PDF?

options.text: As a substitute for current supervised manufacturer training.
As product-specific labeling with version caveats; verify current labeling and institutional protocols.
As a general rule for every LVAD.
As authorization for independent pump adjustment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA-hosted labeling supports device-specific warnings but does not authorize use or replace current training and local protocols.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is a defensible takeaway from the open lung transplant surgical review?

options.text: It defines current transplant candidate listing criteria.
It reviews procurement, preservation and implantation, while candidate selection and donor acceptability are outside its scope.
It authorizes unsupervised procurement.
It says every donor lung is acceptable after recruitment.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The review addresses surgical procedures and explicitly says candidate selection and donor acceptability are discussed elsewhere.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which resource can count toward the 36-hour lecture floor?

options.text: A 10:02 graphic transplant procedure video.
A 10:50 lung-transplant surgical case video.
Only freely accessible didactic recordings with runtime observed and canonical IDs deduplicated; neither procedure case video is a lecture.
An unrendered 8-minute script.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Case demonstrations and plans are not lecture hours. Two public surgical videos have measured durations, but are supplemental procedure videos.

practiceQuestions.stem: An open case report includes age, sex and a rare complication but no explicit de-identification statement. Best course treatment?

options.text: Assume anonymity and copy its video.
Link only, record uncertainty about de-identification, do not copy/rehost media, and avoid unnecessary detail.
Treat open access as image-reuse permission.
Upload the patient record for teaching.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Publication and free viewing do not establish downstream rights to patient images. The case is linked only, with de-identification uncertainty stated.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does completion of this independent course establish?

options.text: Guaranteed board eligibility and procedure competence.
Self-study only; no affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, certification or procedure competence.
Substitution for operative logs.
Certification after passing its questions.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACGME training, supervision, case logs and ABTS certification requirements are separate; course completion grants no credential.

unitMap.text: Access planning and kidney replacement life-plan
coveredTopics: KDOQI ESKD Life-Plan; access referral; multidisciplinary decision and competing-risk framing.
ESKD Life-Plan documentation; changing modality and access goals; why access preferences are individual.

unitMap.text: Vascular anatomy, physical examination, and access surveillance
coveredTopics: Pulse/thrill/bruit; arm edema; dialysis performance; access flow and pressure as contextual signals.
Examination signals listed in KDOQI implementation tool; other causes must be considered; distinguish indicators from diagnosis.

unitMap.text: Duplex ultrasound and maturation assessment
coveredTopics: Gray-scale/color/spectral Doppler; mapping; postoperative maturation; ultrasound guided procedure concepts.
POCUS modes and systematic inflow/conduit/outflow description; maturation mapping; flow measurement and its operator limitations; central-vein blind spots.

unitMap.text: Fistulography, venography, and procedural imaging
coveredTopics: ACR dialysis fistula malfunction variants; access circuit mapping; central outflow assessment.
ACR 2023 variant-specific appropriateness for dysfunction; contrast/radiation and scenario-level limits.

unitMap.text: Stenosis: clinical significance and intervention decision
coveredTopics: KDOQI lesion tools; fistulography; angioplasty/stent-graft decision concepts; recurrence and patency tradeoffs.
KDOQI clinical + angiographic concordance; lesion treatment uncertainty; protect cannulation and future access options.

unitMap.text: Thrombosis, salvage, and access failure
coveredTopics: Absent thrill/pulse; thrombus vs severe stenosis; timing, access history, salvage and fallback planning.
ACR separate suspected thrombosis and intervention variants; urgent team coordination and dialysis contingency.

unitMap.text: Central venous stenosis, occlusion, and catheter complications
coveredTopics: Central venography; CVC dysfunction, fibrin sheath, thrombosis, infection and access preservation.
Central venous disease as a separate ACR variant; duplex limitations and catheter history.

unitMap.text: Aneurysm, pseudoaneurysm, infection, and skin threat
coveredTopics: Access exam, duplex, skin integrity; infection management; aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm pathways.
Skin changes, threatened access, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, infection: recognize red flags and escalate.

unitMap.text: Steal syndrome, ischemia, and high-flow cardiac effects
coveredTopics: Exam with/without access compression as supervised assessment concept; duplex/flow context; surgical vs endovascular consultation.
Steal/ischemia differential; avoid using access flow alone as a diagnostic verdict; multidisciplinary assessment.

unitMap.text: Peritoneal dialysis access and catheter procedures
coveredTopics: PD catheter planning/placement/maintenance; leak, dysfunction, infection; surgery/interventional coordination.
No episode adds procedural detail; access to PD catheter placement is only described at conceptual curriculum level.
Adult PD catheter access and malfunction recommendations: SAGES 2023 and ISPD 2019; conditional/low-certainty evidence; remains a planned, not fully authored episode.

unitMap.text: Temporary dialysis catheter safety, infection prevention, and ultrasound
coveredTopics: ABIM current required procedural experiences; sterile practice, insertion complication recognition, catheter infection prevention.
CDC core infection-prevention measures; distinction between educational knowledge and demonstrated competency.

unitMap.text: Quality, ethics, outcomes, and evidence-based case conference
coveredTopics: Quality/safety, outcomes, source appraisal, case conference synthesis and competency limits.
Source limitations, patient preference, multidisciplinary governance, and honest interpretation of a public service description.

practiceQuestions.stem: A dialysis patient has progressively prolonged post-needle bleeding and rising venous pressures. What is the best next conceptual step?

options.text: Assume stenosis and stent without further assessment
Reassess the clinical access indicators and obtain appropriate access imaging/referral
Ignore findings if the access still has a thrill
Replace the access immediately

practiceQuestions.rationale: Concordant clinical indicators warrant evaluation; intervention is not justified by a single surrogate alone. [KDOQI; ACR]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best characterizes a public fellowship listing for BWH Interventional Nephrology?

options.text: It proves ACGME accreditation for a standalone subspecialty
It is a listed clinical fellowship offering; public sources describe procedural training within nephrology, not its own ACGME specialty
It proves ABIM eligibility in interventional nephrology
It is a research-only postdoctoral position

practiceQuestions.rationale: BWH lists the fellowship; the joint nephrology FAQ describes procedural exposure; ACGME requirements separately concern nephrology fellowship.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fellow wants a board exam specific to interventional nephrology. What is supported?

options.text: ABIM has a separate interventional nephrology board examination
ABIM offers nephrology certification; ASDIN offers procedure-specific certifications, which are not ABMS board exams
ACGME runs the interventional nephrology exam
No nephrology board exam exists

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABIM policy describes nephrology certification and exam; ASDIN describes documentation of procedure-specific certification. No separate ABMS interventional-nephrology board was identified.

practiceQuestions.stem: Fistula thrombosis is suspected because thrill and pulse are absent. Which imaging pathway is ACR-rated usually appropriate to guide intervention?

options.text: MRI without contrast only
Fluoroscopic fistulography; surgical consultation also usually appropriate for treatment
Routine CT without contrast
No evaluation is appropriate

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACR appropriateness guidance for suspected access thrombosis rates fistulography usually appropriate; its treatment variant rates surgical consultation usually appropriate.

practiceQuestions.stem: Ipsilateral arm swelling and venous collaterals occur in a person with dialysis access. What diagnosis must be considered?

options.text: Central venous stenosis or occlusion
Renal artery stenosis
PD peritonitis
AVF maturation only

practiceQuestions.rationale: ACR lists these signs as a clinical suspicion pattern for central venous stenosis/occlusion.

practiceQuestions.stem: A lesion appears on ultrasound but access is functioning well and there are no clinical indicators. Which principle applies?

options.text: Treat every stenosis prophylactically
Interpret imaging with clinical indicators and individualized plan
Use velocity alone as a mandate for stenting
Remove the access

practiceQuestions.rationale: KDOQI emphasizes patient-centered access care and clinically meaningful dysfunction; not every imaging abnormality automatically requires intervention.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which source is the current listed KDOQI vascular access guideline?

options.text: 2019 Clinical Practice Guideline for Vascular Access
2006 hemodialysis adequacy document only
ASDIN exam blueprint
ACR 2003 criteria

practiceQuestions.rationale: NKF identifies its 2019 guideline as current vascular-access recommendations, with implementation tools.

practiceQuestions.stem: What does ASDIN procedure certification mean according to its own description?

options.text: ABMS subspecialty board certification
Documentation that requirements for performance of a particular procedure are met
ACGME accreditation of an institution
State medical license

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASDIN explicitly defines certification as documentation that a physician met specified requirements for a particular procedure.

practiceQuestions.stem: A dialysis catheter patient has fever and rigors during treatment. Which immediate educational priority is best?

options.text: Focus only on elective access mapping
Evaluate for bloodstream infection and follow dialysis infection prevention/escalation protocols
Assume sterile inflammation
Ignore catheter because fistula planning is separate

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC identifies dialysis bloodstream infection as a serious complication and provides core interventions and infection surveillance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A potential learner asks whether this online course confers procedural competence. What is accurate?

options.text: Completion confers competence
Watching procedure videos substitutes for supervised case volume
It provides independent study only; hands-on procedural competence requires supervised institutional training and credentialing
It creates licensure

practiceQuestions.rationale: Neither educational links nor a self-study curriculum replaces clinical supervision, competency assessment, or institutional privileges; ABIM requires supervised clinical competence.

officialProgrammes.institution: Brigham and Women’s Hospital (BWH; Mass General Brigham; Harvard Medical School affiliate)
officialProgrammes.name: BWH Advanced Perioperative Ultrasound and Clinical Anesthesia Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The official MGB directory page that was fetched displays this exact title and labels it “Anesthesiology / Fellowship,” but exposes only a contact link, not an overview, eligibility, rotations, accreditation, active status, or curriculum. The BWH residency page describes its separate residency ultrasound curriculum; it is not evidence for this fellowship curriculum. This programme is preserved as the exact institutional variant in the task packet; current operation and program-specific details remain unverified.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The supplied item packet attributes an official MGB listing to Brigham and Women’s Hospital. The exact MGB-hosted page fetched shows only the BWH title, the labels Anesthesiology/Fellowship, and a contact link; its public text does not say whether the listing is currently recruiting/active, non-ACGME or ACGME-accredited, does not specify prerequisites, duration, rotations or a detailed syllabus. BWH residency is a distinct training program. A separate official BIDMC fellowship has a similar but nonidentical name and detailed one-year non-ACGME clinical scope; it remains a different hospital/programme and is not silently substituted or merged as a BWH variant.
sourceCaveats: The BWH programme page establishes an official named listing only; it is sparse and does not establish active status, accreditation, eligibility or curriculum.
A similar but distinct BIDMC programme was examined to avoid misattribution; it is not a BWH variant.
ABA exams and ACGME programme categories are different from an institution directory’s fellowship heading.
Clinical recommendations can change; the ASRA gastric guidance page states review is due in 2028; the LAST checklist says update expected early 2027. Check live guidance and local policy.

No human clinical review was performed. This is independent education, not medical advice, accredited training, licensure, credentialing, procedure competence, board eligibility, certification or a guarantee of passing.
Utah public page says free access and CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Free viewing does not allow derivative works or rehosting. Counted metadata is a source runtime probe, not proof of learner competency.
PMC extraction was bot-challenged for one source; only its public bibliographic destination is linked, not an unverified quotation.
Original clips are planning only (40 proposed episodes, 1881 target minutes); they have not been recorded/rendered/probed/uploaded and count as zero ready video hours.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which best describes the role of a focused cardiac ultrasound examination?

options.text: It replaces comprehensive echocardiography for any perioperative question.
It answers a narrow, time-sensitive question and must state its limitations.
It confirms a diagnosis whenever one view is adequate.
It should be used only to estimate fluid responsiveness.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FoCUS is a focused bedside subset, not a comprehensive TTE; the operator frames a question and communicates limits. [7,9]

practiceQuestions.stem: A post-induction patient is hypotensive and a focused view appears to show globally reduced LV contraction. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: The cause is definitely cardiogenic shock.
The patient is fluid responsive.
This is an observation to integrate with clinical context and alternative mechanisms.
The patient has acute coronary occlusion.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Gross LV function is one component of a differential and cannot alone establish cause or predict fluid responsiveness. [7]

practiceQuestions.stem: A pericardial effusion is visible on a limited scan. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: Effusion alone establishes tamponade.
Effusion should be described; tamponade requires clinical/hemodynamic interpretation and broader evaluation.
Effusion excludes hypovolemia.
No further review is needed if image is clear.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A visual effusion is not synonymous with tamponade; interpret physiology and escalate when required. [7,9]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which distinction is safest when an ultrasound window cannot be obtained?

options.text: A missing view is a negative examination.
The absent window should be documented as nondiagnostic, not normal.
Repeat probe pressure indefinitely.
Infer the view from the opposite side.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Poor or absent windows do not establish normal anatomy; document quality and limitations. [7]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is an appropriate use of a focused lung view in perioperative care?

options.text: Exclude every cause of hypoxemia.
Add information about pleural/lung findings while integrating ventilation and other data.
Replace chest imaging in all patients.
Diagnose edema from one isolated artifact.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Lung POCUS adds targeted information but artifacts and physiology limit isolated interpretation. [7,8]

practiceQuestions.stem: A limited proximal venous compression scan is negative, but clinical concern for venous thromboembolism remains. What is the best next concept?

options.text: Negative limited scan excludes all DVT.
The scope of a limited scan and clinical context should determine escalation to comprehensive evaluation.
A cardiac scan rules out DVT.
Do not document it.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Limited POCUS is not comprehensive duplex; a negative focused study does not close all diagnostic questions. [7]

practiceQuestions.stem: For a medically complex patient taking a GLP-1 receptor agonist, what is the most accurate summary of the 2025 ASRA gastric POCUS recommendations?

options.text: Routine gastric ultrasound is mandatory for every elective case.
Recommendations are conditional for GLP-1RA use; ultrasound complements judgment and does not replace fasting guidance.
Gastric ultrasound eliminates aspiration risk.
A clear image guarantees safe induction.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASRA 2025 offers conditional support for some groups, including GLP-1RA users, emphasizes individualized clinical judgment and training constraints. [10]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which elements fall within ASA-described TEE scope?

options.text: Probe placement only.
Image acquisition and interpretation only.
Medical necessity, contraindications, placement, acquisition, interpretation, integration, storage, and report.
Only image archiving.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASA statement describes the full scope and recommends appropriate training/credentialing; TEE is invasive. [2]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about the BWH fellowship is supported by the publicly fetched official MGB listing?

options.text: The page publishes its case minimum and ABA-approved syllabus.
The page labels the exact title as Anesthesiology/Fellowship but does not expose a public curriculum or detailed eligibility.
It is an ACGME-accredited ultrasound board fellowship.
It is the same program as BIDMC’s separately titled one-year non-ACGME fellowship.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official BWH listing page exposes the exact title and category but only a contact link; BIDMC is a distinct separate programme. [1,6]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which best describes board recognition for perioperative ultrasound?

options.text: ABA offers a separate ultrasound subspecialty examination.
ABA lists a perioperative ultrasound exam among current subspecialty exams.
The ABA lists several subspecialty examinations, but no separate perioperative ultrasound exam is listed.
The fellowship awards board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABA exam list includes critical care, pain, HPM, sleep, pediatric, neurocritical care, adult cardiac, HALM, but not perioperative ultrasound. [3]

topicGaps: Broad free-flap choice and complex defect-planning lectures remain incomplete: new public recordings are heterogeneous operative/edited examples, not a full, current defect-selection curriculum or supervised skills training.

Flap monitoring has an open review and a tutorial reference, but no newly verified full-length free recording establishing an applicable local protocol or complication-response algorithm; human clinical review is absent.

Current EDX/imaging reasoning (including ultrasound/MRI and serial-testing limits) remains underdeveloped as a complete lecture sequence; no new qualifying free long-form imaging/EDX recording was verified in this expansion.

Neuroma, pain, longitudinal outcome measurement, pediatric/congenital reconstruction and integrated rehabilitation need additional instruction beyond the located recordings and existing open readings; source depth varies.

No separate microsurgery/peripheral-nerve board certificate or dedicated official examination blueprint was located; parent-board competency mapping only, and the distinct hand certificate is not inferred from MGB.
MGB does not publish exact rotations, case volumes, lecture syllabus or an accreditation identifier on its programme page; such clinical-training scope remains unverifiable from that page.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

officialProgrammes.name: Advanced Reconstruction, Microsurgery, and Peripheral Nerve Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official MGB page: 12 months, clinical physician apprenticeship across reconstruction, microsurgery and nerve care; outpatient, inpatient, operative and postoperative experience, multidisciplinary collaboration and research opportunities. No public rotation calendar, case-volume data, lecture syllabus or accreditation identifier is stated.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The supplied packet lists one exact MGB offering; supplemental discovery confirms it. This is an institution-named clinical physician fellowship, not a generic directory label, non-physician supplement or research-only postdoctoral track. Research is an adjunct to stated clinical care. No other institutional variant was verified. MGB page does not by itself establish ACGME accreditation. ACGME publishes Plastic Surgery, Craniofacial Plastic Surgery and Hand Surgery requirements; Hand Surgery is a distinct accredited program, not proof this MGB fellowship is one.
sourceCaveats: MGB programme page is descriptive, not ACGME verification or full curriculum.
ABMS certificate list is evidence for named certificate listings; absence is not a substitute for board confirmation.

2012–2016 WUSTL lectures are educational resources, not current protocols; reconcile clinical decisions with current guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A closed compression injury leaves the nerve in continuity; axons are preserved and recovery occurs as focal conduction block resolves. Which classification best fits?

options.text: Neuropraxia
Axonotmesis
Neurotmesis
Root avulsion

practiceQuestions.rationale: Neuropraxia is focal myelin/conduction dysfunction without axonal discontinuity; classification alone does not guarantee a timeline.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clean sharp nerve transection is confirmed and ends can be approximated without undue tension. Which general reconstructive principle is most supported?

options.text: Favor direct tension-free repair when anatomically appropriate
Force the ends together under tension
Use a long graft in every complete injury
Defer all injuries for six months

practiceQuestions.rationale: Tension-free direct repair is a standard option when feasible; tension and injury context matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A segmental defect cannot be closed without tension. What is the key next reasoning step?

options.text: Compare reconstruction options using gap, nerve type, donor morbidity and evidence
Stretch nerve ends until they meet
Assume a conduit always restores function
Select by a universal length cutoff only

practiceQuestions.rationale: Choice among graft, conduit, allograft and other options depends on more than a single gap size.

practiceQuestions.stem: A proximal mixed motor injury is being evaluated. Why does time-to-target matter?

options.text: Axonal regeneration is slow and distal muscle targets may lose reinnervation opportunity
Motor targets regenerate before axons arrive
Delay has no impact
Sensory responses prove motor recovery

practiceQuestions.rationale: Motor endplate and distance/timing concerns make early, individualized planning important; no universal deadline.

practiceQuestions.stem: A sensory nerve action potential is preserved despite suspected plexus injury. What may it support?

options.text: A preganglionic lesion proximal to the dorsal-root ganglion
Complete distal nerve transection
An isolated tendon rupture
Definitive root avulsion diagnosis by itself

practiceQuestions.rationale: Preserved distal sensory cell bodies/axons can support preganglionic localization, but it is not diagnostic alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which potential advantage is commonly discussed for a selected nerve transfer?

options.text: Shorter distance to target and more direct axon targeting
Elimination of donor morbidity
Guaranteed recovery
No need for rehabilitation

practiceQuestions.rationale: Transfer may shorten reinnervation distance; donor choice, uncertainty and retraining remain.

practiceQuestions.stem: A child in a case series receives processed nerve allograft. Best evidence interpretation?

options.text: An observational small series informs but cannot guarantee individual outcome or universal pediatric standard
The series proves superiority
No consent was needed
The results apply to all injury patterns

practiceQuestions.rationale: A small retrospective series is low-level evidence; populations and follow-up constrain generalization.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which set best describes a clinical free-flap assessment in the cited review?

options.text: Temperature, color, turgor, capillary refill and pin-prick bleeding
Only one monitor number
Routine biopsy at each round
No assessment for buried flap

practiceQuestions.rationale: The review describes this exam while noting visibility and interobserver limitations.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement distinguishes the MGB listing from board qualification?

options.text: It is an official named clinical fellowship; site does not establish a separate microsurgery board exam or accreditation
A fellowship listing guarantees board eligibility
Research opportunities make it research-only
Any completion confers hand certification

practiceQuestions.rationale: Programme, ACGME accreditation and board certification are different source claims.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is required for the ABOS hand certificate pathway per the published page?

options.text: One-year ACGME-accredited hand fellowship plus board/case requirements
Any microsurgery fellowship
A video course
No primary board or case requirements

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABOS page specifies a one-year accredited hand fellowship and additional certification requirements; not inferred for MGB fellowship.

assignment.title: Fictional case conference: adult secondary facial trauma reconstruction
assignment.instructions: Write an anonymized fictional, text-only 1,000–1,500-word case conference. Include problem representation, safety priorities, anatomy/function questions, possible reconstructive categories, shared decision-making considerations, evidence limitations, team needs and follow-up outcomes. Do not include a real patient, clinical image, procedural steps, or patient-specific treatment recommendation.
assignment.rubric: 10 points: safety and priorities 0–2; anatomy and functional reasoning 0–2; alternatives/tradeoffs 0–2; evidence and uncertainty 0–2; patient-centered communication/ethical and credential limits 0–2. Formative threshold 8/10; not a competency test.

topicGaps: Current public runtime remains concentrated in cross-cutting facial/head-and-neck flap content and short trauma/imaging overviews. No verified full-length course covers the MGB-specific adult apprenticeship, aesthetic skeletal contouring, comprehensive composite/bony reconstruction, facial nerve reanimation, outcomes/complications, or an official fellowship-specific board blueprint.

Four public recordings added (three specialty, one supplemental), contributing 1.4744 hours. AMSSM is mapped only as limited conceptual supplement, not specialty-specific runtime. None is an MGB fellowship lecture.
Target remains unmet: 7.8278 verified external hours of 36.0; residual gap 28.1722 hours. Authored scripts are unrendered and count as zero video hours.

AO CMF catalogue reviewed; all access requires login and full library is member-limited. Free, relevant, unrestricted long-form footage at required breadth was not established; further hours require new open recordings or commissioned source-grounded teaching and must not be replaced by guessed duration.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (independent educational course; not training)
boardNames: American Board of Plastic Surgery (ABPS; primary specialty certification)
medical.boardStatus: ACGME currently lists Craniofacial Plastic Surgery as a plastic-surgery subspecialty. The public MGB page describes a 12-month fellowship but does not itself establish this programme’s ACGME accreditation. No separate craniofacial board examination/certificate was identified: ABPS publishes primary plastic-surgery written/oral exams; a 2020 review also states no formal craniofacial certification. Re-check board rules before use. This is not board exam prep.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Completion of plastic surgery residency is the stated MGB applicant requirement, not a promise of eligibility for any board. ABPS alone determines ABPS eligibility. This course confers no eligibility, certification or credential.

officialProgrammes.name: Adult Reconstructive-Aesthetic Craniomaxillofacial Fellowship | Mass General Brigham
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a 12-month adult fellowship emphasizing primary/secondary post-traumatic reconstruction and aesthetic facial skeletal contouring, opportunities for clinical interests/research/teaching, apprenticeship model with Program Director 1:1, and completed plastic surgery residency as prerequisite. No public detailed rotation list or lecture schedule. Preserve exact programme title. Not equivalent to Harvard Plastic Surgery Residency; no separate Hopkins or other institutional variant found in this packet.

medical.programmeSourceScope: One exact institution-specific clinical physician fellowship. Not a generic “craniofacial” directory category, research-only postdoc or non-physician supplement. ACGME subspecialty category does not prove this individual fellowship accreditation.
sourceCaveats: Clinical source checks are dated 2026-10-07; verify current protocols, indications and board rules before teaching.
NCBI pages for some sources returned bot challenges during fetching; access/content caveats are stated at the item level.
No individual MGB ACGME accreditation listing was verified. Public page states 12 months and completed plastic surgery residency prerequisite.
No source establishes a craniofacial-specific board exam; the board exam referenced is primary ABPS plastic surgery certification.
Free-to-view does not allow download, rehosting, figure extraction or reuse. Obtain explicit rights where needed.
Human clinical review is NOT PERFORMED. Independent education only: no affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, operative/procedure competence, certification or pass guarantee.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional adult with major facial trauma, what conceptual priority comes before definitive aesthetic reconstruction?

options.text: Restore facial symmetry immediately
Stabilize life-threatening problems and assess airway/associated injuries
Choose flap based on defect alone
Defer neurologic examination until after closure

practiceQuestions.rationale: Trauma stabilization and screening for associated injury precede definitive reconstruction except where facial injury itself threatens life; plan around patient safety, not appearance alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: Before local anesthesia in a fictional facial laceration case, which finding is especially useful to document when feasible?

options.text: Pre-repair facial motor and sensory function
Final scar color
Late postoperative sensation
Patient’s presumed desired flap

practiceQuestions.rationale: Baseline facial/trigeminal function helps distinguish pre-existing traumatic deficit from later change. This is an educational assessment principle, not a treatment order.

practiceQuestions.stem: A facial defect involves multiple aesthetic units. Which planning principle is most supportable?

options.text: Treat each unit independently regardless of function
Consider unit boundaries and feature-specific perception alongside function and tissue constraints
Always replace with a free flap
Delay all decisions until scar maturation

practiceQuestions.rationale: The facial-trauma review discusses aesthetic-unit planning; choice remains patient- and defect-specific.

practiceQuestions.stem: What is the most accurate description of local flap selection?

options.text: Defect dimensions alone determine design
Geometry, tissue laxity, vascularity, surrounding landmarks, donor morbidity and function all inform planning
A named flap is universally best for cheek defects
Videos establish a learner’s procedural competency

practiceQuestions.rationale: Flap planning is multidimensional; educational videos do not confer supervised operative competence.

options.text: Medical school only

options.text: Assume a single cause and operation
