title: Microsurgery and Breast Reconstruction Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (official institutional offering); independent online course is educational self-study only-aligned independent study

prerequisites.intendedLearner: Plastic-surgery residents/fellows, practicing plastic surgeons and other clinicians studying reconstructive decision-making at an advanced level; patient-facing supplement clearly labeled.
prerequisites.baseline: Completion of medical school and core plastic-surgery residency-level anatomy, oncology, perioperative care and evidence appraisal is assumed. The official MGB fellowship itself requires prior plastic-surgery residency.
prerequisites.notFor: Public self-study does not qualify a learner to select a patient’s treatment, interpret scans as a treating specialist, consent patients, supervise/perform procedures or seek privileges.

objectives: Explain this fellowship’s clinical physician status, public prerequisites and apprenticeship structure while distinguishing programme, ACGME and ABMS claims.
Synthesize oncologic timing, patient goals, implant/autologous alternatives, donor-site factors and multidisciplinary inputs without imposing a universal pathway.
Describe breast/chest-wall and abdominal-wall perforator anatomy and explain what published CTA/3D examples can and cannot establish.
Explain microsurgical flow and complication concepts at a cognitive level, with explicit supervised-practice limits.
Recognize late implant changes as needing clinical evaluation and accurately apply FDA’s current caveats on BIA-ALCL and other capsule-associated malignancies.
Appraise source date, evidence design, image rights and case-report limitations.

units.title: Scope, roles, evidence, safety and the clinical team
objectives: Distinguish the MGB clinical fellowship from a board specialty, ACGME core residency, and independent online self-study.
Frame reconstructive decisions as shared multidisciplinary planning, not a procedural algorithm.
Identify consent, privacy, conflicts of interest, source currency and the limits of public cases.
topics: Fellowship admission prerequisite and apprenticeship model as publicly described
Plastic surgeon, breast surgical oncology, radiation oncology, medical oncology, radiology, pathology, nursing and rehabilitation interfaces

units.title: Oncologic context, timing and reconstruction pathways

units.title: Microsurgical principles, flow and anastomotic reasoning
objectives: Describe microsurgical operating setup and the logic of atraumatic vessel handling, alignment, patency assessment and flow.

units.assessment: Critical-event oral-board-style reasoning checklist: recognize, communicate, gather data, escalate and reassess.

units.title: Postoperative flap monitoring, complications and systems
objectives: Explain why serial monitoring and clear escalation pathways matter after free-tissue transfer.

units.assessment: Handoff scored on completeness, trend clarity, safety language and no invented monitoring cut-offs.

units.title: Radiotherapy integration and oncologic coordination
objectives: Describe why anticipated radiation and reconstructed tissue type matter to multidisciplinary planning.

Documentation of treatment sequence and communication among teams

objectives: Distinguish BIA-ALCL from breast carcinoma and from other reported capsule-associated malignancies.

assignment.title: Reconstruction conference synthesis and evidence audit
assignment.prompt: Using only fictional teaching prompts and the linked public sources, submit a 1,500–2,000 word multidisciplinary planning brief comparing implant-based and autologous pathways for a fictional mastectomy referral with uncertain radiation need, then answer a second fictional late-peri-implant swelling prompt. State what is known, what is missing, who must decide next, how evidence dates/scope affect confidence, and why no online learner should choose or perform a procedure. Do not copy patient images, records, proprietary material or case-report text.
deliverables: Two distinct option maps, not a single operation recommendation
Evidence/source matrix with dates, audience and limitations
One fictional escalation/handoff note for the late swelling scenario
A rights and privacy declaration confirming link-only use of authentic clinical resources

rubric.fullCredit: Uses current sources appropriately, distinguishes patient guide, regulator, guideline and case report; flags dated/limited evidence.
Lists relevant oncology/plastic-surgery/radiation inputs, alternatives, uncertainty and patient goals without prescriptive universal timing.
Recognizes late peri-implant change as requiring clinician assessment, does not diagnose from symptom alone, uses safe escalation language.
Balanced, non-directive, inclusive options; acknowledges trade-offs and values.
No copied patient images/records or proprietary questions; links and source attribution are complete.

assignment.passingRule: 20 points total; 16/20 suggested educational mastery threshold with no critical safety/rights breach. This is not validated, accredited or a credential.

unitMap.text: Scope, roles, evidence, safety and the clinical team
coveredTopics: Fellowship admission prerequisite and apprenticeship model as publicly described
Plastic surgeon, breast surgical oncology, radiation oncology, medical oncology, radiology, pathology, nursing and rehabilitation interfaces
Evidence hierarchy, shared decision-making, informed consent, documentation and safe escalation

unitMap.text: Oncologic context, timing and reconstruction pathways
coveredTopics: Mastectomy envelope, skin- and nipple-sparing context as described in current patient guidance
Implant, autologous, combined, flat closure and delayed pathways
Timing decisions, neoadjuvant/adjuvant treatment and uncertainty of final pathology

unitMap.text: Patient goals, candidacy, risk and informed choice
coveredTopics: Medical and surgical history, body habitus and donor sites
Risk-reduction conversations and individualized assessment
Equity, gender-affirming care, body image, expectations, alternatives and decisional support

unitMap.text: Breast and chest-wall anatomy, mastectomy envelope and perfusion
coveredTopics: Breast/chest wall and internal mammary recipient-vessel context
DIEA branching and perforator course, zone/perfusion concepts at a qualitative level
Mastectomy skin-flap and nipple-areola considerations; anatomy varies between individuals

unitMap.text: Implant-based reconstruction and staged strategies
coveredTopics: Tissue expanders, implant surface/fill, pocket and coverage concepts
Acellular dermal matrix as an adjunct, not a universal requirement
Infection, exposure, contracture, malposition, rupture and revision considerations

unitMap.text: Autologous breast reconstruction: flap options and donor-site trade-offs
coveredTopics: DIEP, SIEA, free/pedicled TRAM and selected gluteal/thigh/latissimus options
Unilateral/bilateral planning, volume, shape, perfusion and donor-site consequences
Flap evidence and patient-centered outcome limitations

unitMap.text: Perforator imaging and preoperative planning
coveredTopics: CTA/3D reconstructions and anatomic variation
Perforator selection variables and image-to-operative communication
Radiation/contrast considerations belong to clinician/radiologist-specific assessment; no generic protocol is prescribed here

unitMap.text: Microsurgical principles, flow and anastomotic reasoning
coveredTopics: Microscope/instrument positioning, tremor control and suture handling
End-to-end/end-to-side concepts and vessel coupling as shown in teaching media
Thrombosis, spasm, kinking, compression and inflow/outflow problems as reasoning categories; clinical rescue follows local protocol and supervisor direction

unitMap.text: Postoperative flap monitoring, complications and systems
coveredTopics: Monitoring principles, handoff and documentation
Flap compromise versus systemic/recipient-site issues
Reoperation/rescue are clinical decisions under local standards and responsible surgeons; not an online procedural manual

unitMap.text: Radiotherapy integration and oncologic coordination
coveredTopics: Postmastectomy radiotherapy and reconstruction sequencing
Autologous abdominal-flap evidence scope and patient-reported outcomes
Documentation of treatment sequence and communication among teams

unitMap.text: Implant-associated malignancy, adverse events and late presentations
coveredTopics: BIA-ALCL, late seroma/mass, pathology-centered evaluation and expert referral
FDA reports of SCC/other lymphomas in implant capsules; uncertainty about cause/incidence/risk factors
Device history, informed consent, routine care and no prophylactic removal recommendation for asymptomatic patients in FDA guidance

unitMap.text: Revision, symmetry, sensation, outcomes and continuous improvement
coveredTopics: Symmetry, fat grafting, nipple/areola reconstruction and revision concepts
Sensory restoration/neurotization as evolving evidence rather than guaranteed result
Patient-reported outcomes, registries, quality review and longitudinal follow-up

topicGaps: Clinical lecture floor remains substantially unfilled: 2.8847 specialty/foundation hours are observed against the 36-hour target, leaving 33.1153 hours. Newly verified free patient/public education is supplemental only and does not meet advanced clinical depth. No qualifying freely accessible long-form specialist recordings were verified for several domains.

Insufficient lecture-level depth remains for oncologic timing and radiation integration; implant-based selection, staged strategies and adverse-event reasoning; flap-family comparison, perforator anatomy/imaging and evidence appraisal; postoperative microsurgical surveillance/escalation; outcomes, sensation and revision; and programme-specific didactics. Existing linked recordings cover only a subset and cannot establish clinical competence.

Two newly verified supplements add patient decision context (Breastcancer.org, 59:06) and a brief hospital microsurgical overview (WVU Medicine, 15:01); both are excluded from the 36-hour specialty/foundation floor. A Johns Hopkins patient webinar remains separately reported as supplementary.

The ChristianaCare public-education candidate returned only a page shell without observed runtime or full description; it remains uncounted. The SURGhub course still requires free-account registration, and its advertised one-hour course is not an observed runtime.

A full-length PRS advanced autologous recording and PRS breast implant ALCL lecture are present in the source ledger but age-restricted; they remain excluded. A separate MedStar operative video was observed as age-restricted and excluded. The 2:17 PRS prepectoral/subpectoral clip is not a full lecture and was not counted.

No separate ABMS/ABPS microsurgery or breast-reconstruction examination was identified in the checked sources; parent plastic-surgery competencies are broad educational mappings only. The MGB page gives no public full didactic schedule or numeric case counts.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (official institutional offering); independent online course is educational self-study only
boardNames: American Board of Plastic Surgery (ABPS) — primary plastic-surgery certification only; no separate microsurgery or breast-reconstruction board exam identified in the checked public sources.
medical.boardStatus: The official MGB offering is a clinical physician fellowship: applicants must have completed a plastic surgery residency, and the page describes sequential two-month apprenticeship blocks with a small number of attendings. The fellowship is not a generic directory label, combined residency, research-only job or non-physician supplement. MGB states that it participates in the San Francisco Match for Microsurgery. ABMS lists ABPS certification in Plastic Surgery and subspecialty certificates in Plastic Surgery Within the Head and Neck and Surgery of the Hand; no separate microsurgery or breast reconstruction certificate/exam is identified on the checked ABMS page. The current ACGME plastic-surgery overview lists Hand Surgery and Craniofacial Plastic Surgery as plastic surgery subspecialties, not microsurgery or breast reconstruction. A 2020 peer-reviewed review described no formal microsurgery certification then; that is a dated secondary source, not a current regulator. No fellowship-specific board exam was located as of the date checked.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: A plastic-surgery residency prerequisite does not establish ABPS exam eligibility. Candidates must independently confirm current requirements with ABPS and the programme/match. This course grants no ABPS eligibility, licensure, accredited training, institutional status or board certification and never guarantees passing.

officialProgrammes.name: Microsurgery and Breast Reconstruction Fellowship | Mass General Brigham
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page says advanced training in breast reconstruction and microsurgery; breast microsurgery is primary focus, with other clinical interests/research/teaching opportunities. Publicly describes a high-volume experience but does not publish case counts or a complete didactic lecture list. Prior plastic surgery residency required; sequential apprenticeship in two-month blocks with a small number of attendings; SF Match participation stated.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Only the exact institutional variant in the input packet was retained: Mass General Brigham, official title and URL as above. The Johns Hopkins seminar linked below is an external patient-facing learning resource, not a Johns Hopkins fellowship. No additional same-specialty institutional variant or combined programme was established by this packet.
sourceCaveats: MGB public page gives high-volume experience but no numeric case counts; none inferred.

MGB does not publish a complete curriculum, rotation/case schedule, ACGME status statement or board pathway on the checked page. ACGME lists core plastic surgery and only the cited subspecialty standards; absence on the overview is not a substitute for live ADS programme-level status verification.
No separate microsurgery/breast reconstruction examination or current ABMS certificate was found in checked authoritative sources. Historical 2020 peer-reviewed analysis is explicitly dated.

ASPS lists the 2013 expander/implant guideline as archived and not publicly accessible; it is not used as current recommendation. The 2017 autologous guideline is linked through a free landing page, while full journal access may be restricted.
The FDA BIA-ALCL Q&A page displays a 2019 content date; the curriculum pairs it with newer 2023 FDA implant-capsule safety communication and the learner should re-check current FDA guidance.

YouTube duration observations are point-in-time public watch-page metadata; availability, age/region rules and publication dates can change. Playlist runtimes may differ by one second from the watch page; direct watch-page runtime was used.

Free-to-view clinical case images are linked only. No diagnostic image, patient record or copyrighted lecture was copied or rehosted. Figure-level reuse and complete de-identification provenance were not independently verified.
SURGhub course is publicly described as free but requires free account registration; actual media access/runtimes were not verified without registration and it is excluded from all hour totals.

Human clinical review is not performed. This independent educational course grants no institutional affiliation, accreditation, medical license, board eligibility, procedural competence or certification.

topicGaps: Clinical lecture floor remains substantially unfilled: 2.8847 specialty/foundation hours are observed against the 36-hour target, leaving 33.1153 hours. Newly verified free patient/public education is supplemental only and does not meet advanced clinical depth. No qualifying freely accessible long-form specialist recordings were verified for several domains.

Insufficient lecture-level depth remains for oncologic timing and radiation integration; implant-based selection, staged strategies and adverse-event reasoning; flap-family comparison, perforator anatomy/imaging and evidence appraisal; postoperative microsurgical surveillance/escalation; outcomes, sensation and revision; and programme-specific didactics. Existing linked recordings cover only a subset and cannot establish clinical competence.

Two newly verified supplements add patient decision context (Breastcancer.org, 59:06) and a brief hospital microsurgical overview (WVU Medicine, 15:01); both are excluded from the 36-hour specialty/foundation floor. A Johns Hopkins patient webinar remains separately reported as supplementary.

The ChristianaCare public-education candidate returned only a page shell without observed runtime or full description; it remains uncounted. The SURGhub course still requires free-account registration, and its advertised one-hour course is not an observed runtime.

A full-length PRS advanced autologous recording and PRS breast implant ALCL lecture are present in the source ledger but age-restricted; they remain excluded. A separate MedStar operative video was observed as age-restricted and excluded. The 2:17 PRS prepectoral/subpectoral clip is not a full lecture and was not counted.

No separate ABMS/ABPS microsurgery or breast-reconstruction examination was identified in the checked sources; parent plastic-surgery competencies are broad educational mappings only. The MGB page gives no public full didactic schedule or numeric case counts.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the official MGB Microsurgery and Breast Reconstruction Fellowship requirements and public curriculum?

options.text: Completion of a plastic surgery residency is required; the page describes sequential two-month apprenticeship blocks with a small number of attendings.
It is an ACGME-accredited one-year residency with an official national breast microsurgery board exam.
Any surgeon may apply without prior plastic-surgery training because it is a research-only programme.
The programme publicly guarantees a specific minimum case volume and board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official page states that applicants must have completed plastic surgery residency and describes two-month apprenticeship blocks. It does not claim an ACGME microsurgery fellowship, separate board examination, or case-volume guarantees.
practiceQuestions.domain: Programme classification, training standards and scope

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner asks whether completing this fellowship alone grants an ABMS subspecialty certificate in microsurgery. Which response is most accurate from the checked sources?

options.text: Yes; the ABMS page lists microsurgery as an ABPS subspecialty certificate.

No separate ABMS microsurgery certificate or board examination was identified; ABMS lists ABPS plastic surgery and relevant separate certificates such as hand surgery and plastic surgery within the head and neck.
Yes; every San Francisco Match fellowship is an ABMS board examination pathway.
No board credentials exist for plastic surgery at all.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABMS’s ABPS page identifies plastic surgery and its listed subspecialties, not microsurgery or breast reconstruction. The ACGME overview likewise lists hand and craniofacial plastic surgery subspecialties. This is a source-checked curriculum statement, not legal advice or a definitive claim about every non-ABMS credential.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a published CTA teaching article, the learner sees a perforator with a relatively short intramuscular segment. What is the best inference?

options.text: It is automatically the vessel that must be selected in every patient.
It is one anatomic feature relevant to planning; selection still requires integration of the individual anatomy and clinical judgment.
It proves that the flap will not develop fat necrosis.
It means CTA should be omitted in all future patients.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Lam et al. describe perforator course and other anatomic features used to support planning. The paper does not make one feature an unconditional rule or guarantee outcome.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient and oncology team are uncertain about postmastectomy radiotherapy. Which online-course response is safest?

options.text: Promise an immediate free flap because it avoids radiation-related issues.
Use a fixed universal waiting interval taken from an old paper.
Describe reconstructive pathways and coordinate individualized timing discussion with breast surgery, radiation oncology and plastic surgery as final oncologic information evolves.
Assume reconstruction cannot be offered after radiation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Timing is an individualized multidisciplinary decision. The available NCCN patient guide and ASTRO guideline describe options and evidence scope, not one interval that should be imposed on every case.
practiceQuestions.domain: Oncologic treatment integration and shared planning

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner compares a small single-institution 3D-assisted DIEP series with a clinical guideline. What appraisal is most appropriate?

options.text: A favorable small series proves the 3D method is superior across all settings.
The series can illustrate a technique and hypothesis; assess patient selection, methods and follow-up, and do not treat it as definitive comparative guidance.
An open-access article is automatically a guideline.
Case series should never be read.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Tomita et al. report 11 unilateral cases. Their series can inform technical concepts but does not establish universal superiority; guideline scope and evidence strength are distinct.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with a breast implant develops new persistent unilateral swelling years after implantation. Which learning point is supported by FDA guidance?

options.text: The swelling alone confirms BIA-ALCL.
Late swelling is a change that warrants clinical evaluation; BIA-ALCL is one concern, but diagnosis requires specialist assessment and appropriate evaluation.
No evaluation is needed if the implant is smooth.
All asymptomatic implants must be removed to prevent lymphoma.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA lists persistent swelling, mass or pain as common BIA-ALCL symptoms and recommends clinical evaluation; symptoms do not themselves establish diagnosis. FDA does not recommend routine removal of implants in asymptomatic patients solely to prevent BIA-ALCL.

practiceQuestions.stem: A student sees an FDA communication about SCC and various lymphomas in breast-implant capsules. Which statement best reflects FDA’s current caution in that page?

options.text: Incidence and causation are known, so all implant patients should have prophylactic capsulectomy.
Reports exist, but cause, incidence and risk factors remain unknown; patients and clinicians should be aware, assess changes and report cases as directed.
These cancers are identical to BIA-ALCL.
The signal is limited to saline-filled implants.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FDA’s March 2023 update reports cases and explicitly says cause, incidence and risk factors remain unknown. It asks for awareness and reporting; it says asymptomatic people do not need implant removal solely for this concern.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which of these is the strongest use of a free public flap-demonstration video in an independent curriculum?

options.text: Use it as evidence that a learner can perform anastomosis independently.
Use it to observe narrated setup and anastomotic concepts, then state that operative competence requires supervised clinical education and assessment.
Use the video as a substitute for a fellowship.
Infer a universally correct technique from the presenter’s demonstration.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A demonstrative lecture supports knowledge visualization but cannot establish skill. ACGME-style workplace training and MGB’s apprenticeship model are distinct from public self-study.
practiceQuestions.domain: Microsurgical principles and scope of video learning

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner wants to reuse a clinical CTA image from an open-access paper in a public course slide. What is the correct first step?

options.text: Copy it because open access means public-domain.
Use the original link for study; verify the specific figure’s license and any patient-consent requirements before reproducing or rehosting it.
Remove the author attribution and crop out labels.
Assume publication makes all images unrestricted.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free-to-view is not permission to reproduce. This course links to authentic published images but copies none; figure-level license and consent must be checked before republication.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately characterizes the public Johns Hopkins “Breast Reconstructive Ladder” webinar used in this curriculum?

options.text: It is a free patient-facing recorded decision webinar, not a Johns Hopkins microsurgery fellowship or board-level clinical curriculum.
It is an accredited clinical residency and is counted as an institutional variant.
Its approximately one-hour runtime is counted as microsurgery specialty lecture time.
It guarantees informed consent or a particular surgical outcome.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official Johns Hopkins page labels it a free recorded webinar guiding the breast reconstructive decision process. Its audience/purpose is patient-facing, so its verified runtime is classified separately as supplemental, excluded from the specialty/foundation floor.
practiceQuestions.domain: Institutional source classification and time accounting
